picks.title: Union3.1: Reducing Systematics in Supernova Cosmology with Self-consistent Measurements of Host Galaxy Properties for 2000 Type Ia Supernovae
picks.abstract: Photometrically derived distances of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) rely on a ∼5% empirical correction based on host galaxy properties, e.g., global stellar mass. Unbiased cosmology inference therefore requires the self-consistent determination of host properties across the full range of redshifts probed, which we undertake here for approximately 2000 SNe in the Union3 compilation (now Union3.1). We use homogeneous optical-infrared photometry from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys to infer global galaxy properties using the stellar population synthesis and SED-fitting code Prospector . We find that the host masses of z < 0.10 SNe in Union3 were on average overestimated, while the opposite was true for z < 0.15 SNe in Pantheon+. After correction, the two studies’ average distance modulus estimated for low-redshift SNe, previously >0.03 mag discrepant, came into 0.01 mag agreement. Updating the UNITY supernova (SN) analysis, we find the uncertainties on all standardization parameters shrink to 0.6–0.9× their previous sizes. For flat Λ cold dark matter (CDM), we find from SNe alone Ω m = 0.34 4 − 0.025 + 0.026 (a −0.4 σ shift from Union3). We then combine with measurements of baryon acoustic oscillations and the cosmic microwave background exactly as done by DESI DR2 and find for flat w 0 w a CDM, w 0 = −0.719 ± 0.084 and w a = − 0.9 5 − 0.26 + 0.29 , corresponding to 3.4 σ evidence against a cosmological constant (down from 3.8 σ per DESI-DR2+Planck+Union3). Updating the DESI-DR2+Planck+SN combined probe analysis with the recent Dovekie recalibration of DES-SN5YR or the updated Pantheon+, we find 3.4 σ (was 4.2 σ before Dovekie) and 3.2 σ (was 2.8 σ before our correction to Pantheon+) evidence, respectively, against a cosmological constant—a significantly improved…

picks.title: Evidence for hidden altermagnetism in Cs 1 − δ V 2 Te 2 O
picks.abstract: Altermagnets are characterized by anisotropic band/spin splittings in momentum space, dictated by their spin-space group symmetries. However, the real-space modulations of altermagnetism are often neglected and have not been explored experimentally. Here we combine neutron diffraction, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), spin-resolved ARPES and density functional theory to demonstrate that Cs_(1-δ)V₂Te₂O realizes a spatially modulated form of altermagnetism, i.e., hidden altermagnetism. Such a state in Cs_(1-δ)V₂Te₂O results from its G-type antiferromagnetism and two-dimensional electronic states, allowing for the development of spatially alternating altermagnetic layers, whose local spin polarizations are directly verified by spin-resolved ARPES measurements. Our experimental discovery of hidden altermagnetism broadens the scope of unconventional magnetism and opens routes to exploring emergent phenomena from real-space modulations of altermagnetic order.

picks.title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
picks.abstract: Large and giant double-stranded DNA viruses substantially affect eukaryotic ecology and evolution 1–4 . They prevail in the environment but are rarely found in the digestive system of animals 5,6 . Here we present the discovery of a diversified group of DNA viruses with large linear genomes, dubbed egoviruses, that comprise a putative viral order most closely related to animal-infecting poxviruses. Egoviruses are found worldwide, almost exclusively in the digestive system of humans, livestock and wild animals. The most prevalent human-specific egovirus is spread across continents, demonstrating a long-term association between egoviruses and the human gut microbiome. Eukaryotic homologues of egovirus core genes suggest that these viruses primarily infect Trichostomatia (ciliates), which assist ruminant digestive processes 7 , and Parabasalia (Metamonada), which influence animal immunity and gut microbiome ecology 8 . Egoviruses also contributed to the genetic makeup of polintons, endogenous viruses that proliferated in genomes of Trichomonas vaginalis 9 and its close Parabasalia relatives. Unlike poxviruses that form brick-shaped virions, egoviruses are predicted to form multilayered icosahedral capsids resembling those of asfuviruses and probably representing the ancestral virion structure. Egoviruses are the only known clade of double-stranded DNA viruses of eukaryotes prevailing in the animal digestive system. Phylogenomic analysis suggests an evolutionary scenario whereby egovirus-like ancestors of poxviruses infected anaerobic unicellular eukaryotes inside the gut of ancestral animals, before transitioning to animal cell infection, which was accompanied by the virion metamorphosis.

picks.title: Noise-Driven Odd Elastic Waves in Living Chiral Active Matter
picks.abstract: Chiral active matter is predicted to exhibit odd elasticity, with nontraditional elastic response arising from a combination of chirality, being out of equilibrium, and the presence of nonreciprocal interactions. One of the resulting phenomena is the possible occurrence of odd elastic waves in overdamped systems, although its experimental realization still remains elusive. Here we show that in overdamped active systems, noise is required to generate persistent elastic waves. In the chiral crystalline phase of active matter, such as that found recently in populations of swimming starfish embryos, the noise arises from the self-driving of active particles and their mutual collisions, a key factor that has been missing in previous studies. We identify the criterion for the occurrence of noise-driven odd elastic waves and construct the corresponding phase diagram, which is also applicable to general chiral active crystals. Our results can be used to predict the experimental conditions for achieving a transition to self-sustained elastic waves in overdamped active systems.

picks.title: Deciphering the Physical Origin of GRB 240825A: A Long Gamma-Ray Burst Lacking a Bright Supernova
picks.abstract: We present a comprehensive multiwavelength analysis of GRB 240825A, a bright gamma-ray burst (GRB) detected by Fermi and Swift, with a prompt duration ( T 90 ∼ 4 s in the 50–300 keV band measured by the Gamma-ray Burst Monitor) near the boundary separating short and long GRBs, prompting a detailed investigation into its classification and progenitor. We use classical prompt metrics (duration, minimum variability timescale, lag, and spectral hardness) and modern classification techniques (machine learning–based t-SNE, support vector machine, energy- hardness duration, and ε ≡ E γ , iso , 52 / E p , z , 2 5 / 3 ) and find most properties (prompt energetics, placement on the Amati relation, and spectral lag) of GRB 240825A consistent with a collapsar origin. However, extensive late-time optical and near-infrared follow-up with the 10.4 m Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC) telescope and the 8.4 m Large Binocular Telescope reveals no bright supernova (SN; like SN 1998bw) is detected down to stringent limits (e.g., m r > 25.0 mag at 17.59 days), despite a redshift of z = 0.659 measured from GTC spectroscopy. Host-galaxy spectral energy distribution modeling with Prospector indicates a massive, star-forming galaxy typical of collapsar GRB hosts, though with a large offset. We compare these findings with hybrid events like GRB 211211A, GRB 230307A, GRB 200826A, including supernovae-GRBs, and conclude that GRB 240825A most likely originated from a massive star collapse, possibly with the associated AN heavily obscured or intrinsically faint. This study emphasizes the need for multiwavelength follow-up and a multilayered classification to determine GRB progenitors.

picks.title: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits
picks.abstract: Photonic integrated circuits are emerging as a key technology for compact, analogue and energy-efficient optical information processing 1 . Yet, their practical implementation remains limited by the intrinsically weak optical nonlinearities of conventional materials, which demand high power and large device footprints to achieve substantial nonlinear responses 2 . Exciton–polaritons, hybrid light–matter excitations of semiconducting materials, offer a promising route to overcome these limitations by combining strong optical nonlinearities with the high speed and scalability typical of photonic platforms 3–5 . However, despite their potential, fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification have remained elusive. Here we demonstrate a fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings these functionalities together in a single-step-grown platform. We realize precise and scalable polariton circuits with integrated gratings that act as both couplers and reflectors, enabling in-plane Fabry–Pérot cavities. These structures support robust in-plane polariton lasing with coherent guided emission at a geometry-defined wavelength, optical amplification of propagating polaritons and nonlinear optical phase control exceeding π, all within the same on-chip architecture. Our results establish perovskite polariton circuits as a scalable platform for active and interferometric integrated photonics.

picks.title: De Novo Folding Mechanisms of Lasso Peptides
picks.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
picks.abstract: Lasso peptides adopt a distinctive [1] rotaxane conformation, yet the principles governing the folding of this kinetically trapped structure have remained elusive. Here, we integrated extensive molecular dynamics simulations and deep learning to elucidate the de novo folding mechanism of 20 lasso peptides lacking secondary post-translational modifications. We constructed Multi-Ensemble Markov Models for each lasso peptide and uncovered a consistent uphill folding landscape with spontaneous folding probabilities below 0.8%. Loop stability strongly correlated with folding propensity. Both simulations and experiments suggested that enhancing loop β-hairpin formation promotes folding of microcin J25, the well-studied lasso peptide extensively characterized as an in vitro model. This was confirmed by in silico loop-swap chimeras: grafting the microcin J25 loop onto the structurally similar klebsidin conferred prefolded stability. Leveraging Variational AutoEncoder-based pathway clustering, we resolved distinct pathway channels and representative folding pathways, further supporting this conclusion from a kinetic perspective. Additionally, a substantial entropy penalty was found to oppose lasso peptide folding. Simulations mimicking enzymatic spatial confinement reduced this penalty and stabilized the prefolded state. Together, these findings establish representative folding models and fundamental thermodynamic and kinetic principles which may be applied toward the rational engineering of lasso peptides.

picks.title: Cooperative Heterogeneous–Homogeneous Catalysis Enables Aprotic H2O2 Synthesis and Tandem Organic Oxidations
picks.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
picks.abstract: We show that cooperation of heterogeneous metal and homogeneous Brønsted-acid catalysts enables direct synthesis of hydrogen peroxide (H2 + O2 → H2O2) in aprotic solvents. By studying different molecular acids, we discover that the selectivity of H2O2 vs H2O formation is controlled by the steric profile of the acid, which we hypothesize orchestrates the formation of transition states for proton-coupled reduction of metal-bound O2. This mechanistic understanding informs our selection of unhindered Brønsted-acid catalysts that tune H2O2 selectivity by ∼20× in aprotic acetonitrile solvent on Pd/C catalysts. We show the synthetic value of H2O2 formation in organic solvents by addition of a third catalytic function via titanium silicalite-1 (TS-1) zeolite that activates H2O2 to oxidize thioanisole into the corresponding sulfoxide and sulfone. This work thus establishes strategies for tunable heterogeneous–homogeneous catalytic cooperativity and synthetic protocols for peroxide-mediated oxidation of organic substrates.

picks.title: Designed broken symmetries facilitate configurational complexity in nematic vortex crystals
picks.abstract: Although widely used in modern technological applications, liquid crystals have not yet been systematically explored or utilized as reconfigurable information storage devices. Here we demonstrate that precisely designed broken symmetries in nematic vortex crystal lattices give rise to exponential configurational complexity exceeding the configurational entropy of conventional atomic crystals, and arising from the manifold ways in which surface-anchored nematic defect lines can combine to form nematic vortex crystals with distinct free-energy minima and tailored broken symmetries, thereby generalizing the interstitial and substitutional defects as well as grain boundaries in conventional crystalline materials. We illustrate the versatility of our experimental platform by designing nematic vortex crystals with various broken symmetries and show how their topological states can be reconfigured on demand via laser-induced topological surgery. Thus, our results provide an experimental and conceptual foundation for the development of soft-matter-based topological memory and computation devices.

picks.title: The Seeds of State Capture: Merit and Patrimonialism in the Colonial Bureaucracy
picks.abstract: Bureaucracies vary in the extent to which hiring is meritocratic versus patrimonial. Such outcomes are typically seen as the result of politicians’ behavior. However, politicians often delegate hiring to existing bureaucrats. When political leaders are socially distant from communities they seek to govern and these areas are peripheral to politicians’ core interests, bureaucrats’ private preferences can dominate hiring decisions instead. Colonial and other forms of external state-building typify cases where patrimonialism created by bureaucrats, not politicians, can emerge. Digitizing individual-level records across six decades of British rule in Ghana, we find evidence of patrimonialism rather than meritocracy in the hiring of African staff, with large inequities across ethnic groups. Our results demonstrate the underexplored agency of local bureaucrats in state-building and highlight conditions under which bureaucrats’ preferences, rather than only political principals’, shape state institutions. They also challenge conventional wisdom about why, and when, newly-independent African states became “neopatrimonial.”

more.title: First Indication of Low-Energy Solar Neutrino-Electron Scattering with PandaX-4T Run 2 Data
more.abstract: We report a search for the solar proton–proton ( p p ) neutrino flux via neutrino–electron elastic scattering using the PandaX-4T Run 2 data set collected between 2024 and 2026, corresponding to an exposure of 1.9 tonne ⋅ yr. Before Run 2 data taking, the detector underwent a series of upgrades to improve its response and background conditions. Time variations of radioactive noble-gas impurities are constrained using the physics data themselves, complemented by measurements from the gas-assay system. The analysis introduced improvements in the data processing chain, detector response characterization, and background models. A blind spectral analysis was then performed on the electronic-recoil data across a wide energy range from 20 to 1000 keV. In combination with the Run 0 data published earlier, the pp neutrino flux is derived to be ( 8.5 ± 3.5 ) × 10 10 c m − 2 s − 1 , consistent with the prediction of the Standard Solar Model. The combined dataset yields a 2.2 σ statistical significance for solar neutrino-electron scattering, representing the first positive indication obtained using data below the Borexino analysis threshold of 165~keV.

more.title: Mind the gap: Anti-critical quantum metrology
more.abstract: Critical quantum metrology exploits the dramatic growth of the quantum Fisher information near quantum phase transitions to enhance the precision of parameter estimation. This enhancement is commonly associated with a closing energy gap, which causes the characteristic timescales for adiabatic preparation or relaxation to diverge with increasing system size. As a consequence, the apparent growth of the quantum Fisher information largely reflects the increasing evolution time induced by critical slowing down rather than a genuine improvement in metrological performance, thereby limiting the practical usefulness of such protocols. Here we show that the relationship between energy gaps, quantum correlations, and achievable precision in interacting quantum systems can be far more subtle. In particular, quantum-enhanced sensitivity can also emerge when the energy gap increases, eliminating critical slowing down and enabling substantially faster relaxation dynamics. Although the corresponding quantum Fisher information may decrease due to the shorter evolution time, the resulting precision can nevertheless remain quantum-enhanced. Building on this insight, we introduce an anti-critical quantum metrology scheme in which quantum-enhanced precision arises while the energy gap grows. We illustrate this mechanism using the quantum Rabi model, thereby identifying a route to metrological advantage that avoids the slow dynamics associated with conventional criticality.

more.title: Observability of Eccentricity in a Population of Merging Compact Binaries
more.abstract: We investigate the prospects of observing residual eccentricity in a population of compact binaries by calculating the power in the eccentric harmonics, following the methodology in B. G. Patterson et al. Although most observed compact binary coalescences are expected to circularize before entering the sensitivity band of the ground-based gravitational wave (GW) detectors, dynamical interactions in dense star clusters can lead to a fraction of these binaries with nonnegligible eccentricity at the time of detection. To quantify the observability of eccentricity, we simulate a population of merging compact binaries and identify those that have sufficient power in subdominant eccentric harmonics to be clearly distinguishable from quasi-circular systems. We consider a binary black hole (BBH) population derived from globular cluster (GC) simulations with residual eccentricity distribution obtained from Cluster Monte Carlo (CMC) catalogs as well as a fiducial log-uniform model. Assuming the LIGO-Virgo network of GW detectors with their sensitivities achieved during the fourth Observing Run (VK), we find that the BBH population with measurable eccentricity will have a significantly higher median eccentricity e 10Hz ∼ 0.3 (with 90% range: 0.1−0.6) and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) ∼ 20 (90% range: 13−54) compared to the observable population of BBHs. We compare our predictions of the regions of parameter space where eccentricity is detectable with the claimed observations of eccentricity in GW events from the third Gravitational Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC-3).

more.title: Soft contributions stabilize next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD corrections to quarkonium production and decay
more.abstract: Next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) QCD corrections to quarkonium production and decay are known to exhibit perturbative instabilities within non-relativistic QCD. We identify the origin of this problem and propose a simple remedy. Applying our approach to S-wave color-singlet quarkonium processes, we achieve substantially improved perturbative convergence and agreement with experimental data.

more.title: Host–microbe interactions in engineered immunocompetent human gut tissues
more.abstract: The intestinal mucosal barrier contains microbial organisms within the lumen while preserving the ability to absorb nutrients. Dietary, microbial, and other exposures shaped human barrier evolution and continue to impact disease susceptibility. Here, we established engineered barrier models of the human small intestine and colon composed of a multilineage epithelium, mucus layer, accessible microbial compartment and autologous tissue-resident immune cells. The epithelium has crypt- and villus-like topological domains, with stem cells differentiating into absorptive and secretory lineages with region-specific identities. Secreted mucins accumulate apically, forming a dense mucus layer separating the epithelium from colonizing commensal and pathogenic bacteria. Intestinal memory T cells integrate into and interact with the epithelium. We use the engineered intestinal tissues to identify an epithelial gene regulatory network underlying response to Salmonella Typhimurium infection, and uncover epithelial-immune-pathogen crosstalk coordinating cytokine release and epithelial damage. Overall, this work allows for the modular integration of epithelial, microbial, and immune compartments providing a versatile system for studying human intestinal physiology and pathologies.

more.title: Fully Nonequilibrium Hall Response from Berry Curvature
more.abstract: In topological materials, Berry curvature leads to intrinsic Hall responses. Focusing on time-reversal symmetric systems with broken inversion symmetry, a spontaneoous (zero magnetic field) Hall effect is expected to develop under an applied electric field. Motivated by recent developments in Weyl-Kondo semimetals, here we advance a fully nonequilibrium (FNE) Hall response due to the Berry curvature. In particular, we show that, while the spontaneous Hall current is quadratic in the previously described regime of weak electric field, due to the contribution from the dipole moment of the Berry curvature, the FNE Hall response for non-perturbative electric fields is not controlled by the Berry curvature dipole. Remarkably, the FNE Hall response resembles what happens in systems that break the microscopic time-reversal symmetry. We illustrate the universality of these results by comparing them with their counterparts in systems with any higher-multipole of the Berry curvature. The implications of our results for the understanding of strongly correlated topological semimetals are discussed.

more.title: A Comparative Study of the Streaming Instability: Unstratified Models with Marginally Coupled Grains
more.abstract: The streaming instability is a leading mechanism for concentrating solids and initiating planetesimal formation in protoplanetary disks. Although numerous studies have explored its linear growth, nonlinear evolution, and implications for planet formation, the diversity of numerical methods and dust treatments used across the literature has made it difficult to assess which features of the instability are physically robust and which arise from code-dependent choices. We present the first systematic comparison of seven hydrodynamic codes—spanning finite-volume and finite-difference schemes and modeling dust either as Lagrangian particles or as a pressureless fluid—applied to the unstratified streaming instability with a dimensionless stopping time of unity. All codes reproduce the characteristic sequence of exponential growth, filament formation, and turbulent saturation, demonstrating broad agreement in the qualitative behavior of the instability. Quantitatively, however, the dust model remains the dominant source of variation at moderate resolution; particle-based simulations reach higher peak densities and exhibit broader high-density tails than fluid-based models at 512 2 resolution, although increasing the number of particles brings their initial maximum density evolution into close agreement with that of dust-fluid models. At 1024 2 , these differences diminish substantially, indicating better agreement of the saturated-state statistics across dust treatments. In terms of computational performance, most particle implementations suffer from imbalanced parallelized loads, while execution on a GPU is at least 2–3 times more energy efficient and scales better at higher resolutions than on CPUs. more.title: Global patterns and drivers of bee richness and endemism on islands
more.abstract: Islands harbor a disproportionate share of global biodiversity 1 , yet insects, even invaluable pollinators such as bees 2 , remain underrepresented in island biogeography research 3 . Here, we present the first global checklist of island bees, recording 4,140 species across 306 islands. Although islands comprise only ∼5% of Earth’s land area, they support ∼20% of global bee diversity, and 43% of insular species are endemic, making up ∼8% of all known bee species. Island bee species richness, mirroring continental trends 4 , peaks at mid-latitudes. Native richness increases with island area and declines with isolation, consistent with patterns in other taxa 5 . The strength of species–area relationships varies among biomes and is steepest in mediterranean-type systems, which also support disproportionately high bee richness relative to flowering plant diversity. Endemism is highest on large tropical islands, reflecting extensive in situ diversification. Major centers of bee endemism include Madagascar, Malesia (e.g. the Greater Sundas and New Guinea), and Hawai’i, where a single large radiation of Hylaeus ( Nesoprosopis ) dominates 6 . Among islands capable of supporting endemic species, endemism scales strongly with total richness. These findings highlight the need to integrate island bee diversity into global conservation planning and position bees as a model for understanding insect evolution and conservation on islands.

more.title: Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
more.abstract: Quantum field theories provide fundamental models of complex interacting systems 1–3 , from high-energy physics and cosmology to condensed matter. However, solving these models in non-perturbative and dynamical regimes is often challenging, particularly in more than one spatial dimension. Analogue simulation using tunable synthetic quantum systems can both verify existing theoretical predictions and lead to physical insights. Here we realize analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions (two spatial dimensions and time), using two coherently coupled spin components 4,5 in a uniform two-dimensional atomic Bose–Einstein condensate 6,7 . Specifically, we encode the paradigmatic sine-Gordon model 8,9 in the long-wavelength modes of the field describing the relative phase, ϕ , of the two components. In the perturbative regime, collective field excitations exhibit a relativistic dispersion with a tunable mass gap. We also observe explicitly non-perturbative phenomena, including the existence of topological domain walls across which ϕ rapidly winds by 2π (ref. 10 ). Our work opens possibilities for studies of cosmologically relevant phenomena including preheating 11,12 , dynamics of topological defects 13,14 and relativistic false-vacuum decay 15–19 .

more.title: DIISC-VII: Linking Radial Gas Motions to Anomalously Low-metallicity Star-forming Regions in the XUV Disk of NGC 3344
more.abstract: We present evidence connecting anomalously low-metallicity regions to radial gas inflows in the extended ultraviolet (XUV) disk of the galaxy NGC 3344. Anomalously low-metallicity H ii regions are hypothesized to result from the accretion of metal-poor gas, but a direct link between gas flows and low-metallicity gas has not been previously established. We use high-resolution H i 21 cm imaging from the Very Large Array to trace neutral gas kinematics and multislit optical spectroscopy from the MMT to trace the gas-phase metallicity of 76 H ii regions in NGC 3344. The galaxy exhibits a negative radial metallicity gradient of −0.378 dex R 25 − 1 , with H ii regions in the XUV disk showing nearly twice the metallicity scatter of those in the inner disk and several showing an anomalously low metallicity. Modeling the H i disk as tilted rings with 3D BAROLO, we find gas moving radially inward within the XUV disk at an average radial velocity of 6 km s −1 , likely fueling star formation and diluting the metallicity, thereby producing anomalously low-metallicity regions. Chemical evolution models indicate that the gas fraction, effective yield, and mass-loading factor profiles are disrupted at the onset of the XUV disk, as expected from recent gas flows. This example is the first direct detection of how radial gas flows can support stellar disk expansion and cause inside-out galaxy growth.

more.title: Confidently Wrong: Why Ignoring Binaries Biases IMF Inference at Large Sample Sizes
more.abstract: The stellar initial mass function (IMF) high-mass slope α is routinely measured by fitting single-star models to photometric samples that contain unresolved binaries. This practice introduces a systematic negative bias on α that is constant with sample size N . Posterior credible intervals shrink as 1 / N , so at sufficiently large N the bias exceeds the full 95% credible interval width and the true value falls outside the credible interval—a regime we call “confidently wrong.” Building on earlier studies of the bias magnitude, we quantify the sample size at which this bias exceeds the statistical uncertainty. We quantify this bias using two idealized observation operators: mass addition ( m obs = m 1 + m 2 ), a formal upper bound on unresolved system mass overestimation, and luminosity addition ( m obs = L −1 ( L 1 + L 2 )), an idealized lower bias photometric case based on the zero-age main sequence mass–luminosity relation. Across four astrophysical environments spanning α = 1.60–2.30 we find: (1) mass addition bias of 0.054–0.086 with crossover to confidently wrong at N cross ∼ 5000–10,000; (2) luminosity addition bias of 0.011–0.021 with N cross ∼ 75,000–150,000; and (3) a binary-aware mixture likelihood that marginalizes over the M. Moe & R. Di Stefano binary population model, which recovers the true slope in the synthetic tests presented here. Published single-star IMF slopes can therefore plausibly carry systematic errors of orders of 0.01–0.09 if unresolved binaries are not modeled, comparable to or exceeding reported uncertainties in some regimes. Since current and upcoming surveys (Gaia, JWST, Roman, and LSST) will deliver large resolved-star samples, binary-aware inference is likely necessary to avoid binary-driven systematic bias in the large- N…

more.title: Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids
more.abstract: Resistance in standard conductors decreases with increasing cross-section. Yet, in low-dimensional superconductors and superfluids, residual resistance arises from topological fluctuations of the order parameter, manifesting as phase slips in one-dimensional (1D) and vortices in two-dimensional (2D) systems. How resistance and dissipation evolve as geometry interpolates between these regimes remains an open question. This evolution is masked in solid-state experiments by disorder, impurities and geometric imperfections 1–3 , and poses theoretical challenges due to competing dissipative processes and pronounced finite-size effects. Here, we use a defect-free unitary Fermi gas in a digitally programmable transport geometry to isolate geometric effects on superfluid dissipation and discover a paradox: in the crossover from one dimension to two dimensions, the resistance reaches a minimum. There, widening a channel increases its resistance. Narrower, quasi-1D channels show dissipation described by Langer–Ambegaokar–McCumber–Halperin theory of phase slips 4 . In this regime, varying the channel width yields the predicted exponential scaling of the activation factor over many orders of magnitude. Wider, quasi-2D channels show dissipation consistent with phase-slip events described by a finite-size vortex model 5 . The minimal dissipation in the dimensional crossover reflects a transition in the dominant dissipative mechanism, with both 1D and 2D events simultaneously suppressed. Our measurements suggest a route to minimizing dissipation in superconducting devices and provide a benchmark for theoretical efforts aimed at describing the dimensional crossover.

more.title: Mesoporous Defect-Assisted Ce-Doped Cu-SSZ-13 Enabling Low-Temperature NH3–SCR via Enhanced Oxygen Transfer
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Coupling efficient redox cycling with molecular diffusion in confined microporous environments remains a central challenge in zeolite catalysis. In Cu-exchanged SSZ-13 catalysts for NH3-assisted NOx reduction, low-temperature activity is limited by sluggish Cu redox interconversion and mass-transport constraints, while incorporation of secondary cations often intensifies pore-diffusion penalties. Herein, we show that defect-mediated mesostructuring enables the stable incorporation of atomically dispersed Ce species within Cu-SSZ-13, forming a Cu–Ce adjacent structure that synergistically modulates transport and redox chemistry. In situ spectroscopic and isotope-labeling analyses combined with multiscale simulations reveal that the engineered defect network enhances NOx and NH3 diffusion, while Ce species anchored at defect-edge sites promote oxygen activation and accelerate Cu-NO2 intermediate formation. These effects collectively facilitate more efficient Cu2+/Cu+ cycling across a substantially broadened temperature window. The resulting catalyst achieves ≥90% NOx conversion between 147 and 560 °C. More broadly, this work establishes defect-enabled secondary-cation stabilization as a promising strategy to decouple diffusion limitations from redox optimization in confined catalytic systems.

more.title: The Overprediction Problem: Aligning Computational Crystal Structure Prediction with Experimental Reality for Two Sulfa Drugs
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Computational crystal structure prediction (CSP) methods usually overpredict the number of plausible polymorphs. In this study, we used sulfadiazine (SDZ) and sulfamerazine (SMZ), which are respectively monomorphic and pentamorphic (by the end of this study), to investigate the extent of CSP overprediction and its use in designing experiments that identify additional polymorphs. Lattice energy CSP studies (CSP_0) generate a few hundred plausible crystal structures (low-energy minima) for these molecules; however, if these crystal structures are simulated at ambient conditions using a molecular dynamics workflow, then many of the structures can be clustered as equivalent, reducing the number of distinct structures by about 60%. The relative energies are refined using a variety of periodic DFT+D and phonon calculations on the competitive structures. Comparison of the known and CSP-generated thermodynamically competitive structures suggests that forming solid solutions or subliming onto template crystals could enable the discovery of new forms. Solid solutions with the predicted structure of SMZ-IV were found, with SDZ content ranging from 30% to 70%. The combined computational and experimental study suggests that SDZ is monomorphic and that SMZ form II is the low-temperature stable form, enantiotropically related to the polymorphs I, III, and V of SMZ due to the unusual thermal stabilization of a layer structure that occurs in the most readily crystallized form I. The contrasting polymorphisms of SMZ and SDZ illustrate the reasons for overprediction and the requirements for polymorph prediction by CSP.

more.title: A Ferrielectric Quasi-Racemic Crystal from an Enantiopolar Racemate
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Ferrielectrics, materials with partly switchable polarization, enable functional responses such as pyroelectricity and piezoelectricity. However, general design strategies for purely organic ferrielectric crystals remain scarce. Here we show that quasiracemates (QR), derived from enantiopolar centrosymmetric racemates, may provide a novel route to organic ferrielectrics. In these structures, quasi-enantiomers assemble into antiparallel polar columns that reveal the hidden polarization of the parent racemate. We hypothesized that a quasi-enantiomer bearing an acidic proton capable of forming an additional hydrogen bond could enable ferrielectric switching. Guided by this principle, we designed a QR composed of N-Ac-R-Val and N-Ac-S-Thr. The obtained crystals exhibit P21 symmetry and display ferrielectric characteristics, along with a large absolute pyroelectric coefficient (∼3.9 × 10–9 C/(K·cm2)) and a relatively low absolute piezoelectric response (d22 ∼ 2.27 pm/V). Deuteration of the acidic protons suppresses both the large pyroelectric response and the ferrielectric switching, providing strong evidence that these phenomena are driven by these protons and their local hydrogen-bonding environment. The macroscopic polarization and polar properties are further tunable by doping N-Ac-RS-Val with varying concentrations of N-Ac-S-Thr.

more.title: A Tailor-Made Guanidine Ionizable Lipid as a Bifunctional mRNA Carrier and Nitric Oxide Production Inhibitor
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the leading clinical platform for mRNA delivery, yet their capacity to trigger macrophage-driven inflammatory responses remains a fundamental barrier to therapeutic safety and efficacy. Here, we introduce a design principle in which a tailor-made nitric oxide (NO) inhibitory motif is embedded directly into the ionizable lipid, creating a single molecular scaffold that simultaneously delivers mRNA and suppresses macrophage inflammation. Screening of a focused acyl-guanidine library in LPS-induced peritoneal macrophages identified G9 as a potent NO inhibitor and reprogrammed macrophage polarization from the pro-inflammatory M1 to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. Conjugation of the G9 headgroup to a lipid tail yielded G9-1, an NO-inhibitory ionizable lipid that retains anti-inflammatory activity and preferentially delivers mRNA to pulmonary vascular endothelial cells and alveolar macrophages in vivo. In a murine model of acute lung injury (ALI), G9-1 LNPs loaded with IL-10 mRNA reduce pulmonary immune cell infiltration, suppress inflammatory cytokine production, and attenuate systemic inflammation. These results establish NO inhibition as an actionable molecular design principle for intrinsically anti-inflammatory LNPs and position G9-1 as a dual-function ionizable lipid for safer and more effective mRNA therapeutics.

more.title: TMEM184 proteins are Ca 2+ uptake transporters in lysosomes
more.abstract: Lysosomal Ca 2+ release from acidic stores is critical for lysosomal function, yet the molecular identity of the Ca 2+ uptake conduit has remained elusive. We used a Ca 2+ -imaging–based genetic screen of the lysosomal membrane proteome to identify TMEM184 family proteins as lysosomal Ca 2+ transporters (LyCaTs) essential for Ca 2+ uptake and refilling. TMEM184 selectively transported Ca 2+ while excluding monovalent cations. Loss of TMEM184B/C depleted lysosomal Ca 2+ stores, diminished Ca 2+ release, and disrupted lysosomal exocytosis, biogenesis, and membrane repair, thus phenocopying the release channel transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) deficiency. Moreover, a human TMEM184B mutation associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder compromised lysosomal Ca 2+ transport, and Tmem184b -deficient mice exhibited profound motor impairment. Thus, TMEM184 constitutes the long-sought Ca 2+ uptake and refilling mechanism that governs lysosomal signaling and homeostasis.

more.title: The cryosphere beyond a planetary safe operating space
more.abstract: The cryosphere plays a vital role in regulating planetary dynamics and habitability, yet it remains unclear whether its essential functions remain within a safe operating space (SOS) amid Anthropocene change. Here, we propose a cryosphere SOS and systematically evaluate its contributions to Earth system resilience using the planetary boundaries framework. Multiple lines of evidence indicate an accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity, driven by amplifying feedbacks. Key cryospheric control variables either have left or are committed to departing from Holocene-like conditions. We conclude that the cryosphere has breached its SOS and is on a trajectory that locks in long-term risks for human societies and ecosystems. Safeguarding planetary resilience therefore requires explicit consideration of cryosphere change and its interactions across the Earth system.

more.title: Geodetic observations in West Antarctica reveal geodynamically consistent 3D mantle viscosity
more.abstract: The rapid ice loss in West Antarctica since the 1990s has led to substantial ice surface lowering, regional bedrock uplift, and gravity reduction, as measured by geodetic observations. The bedrock (crustal) motions and gravity changes result from glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA), a process controlled by Earth's viscoelastic properties and deglaciation history. In this study, we present GIA models with geodynamically consistent three-dimensional mantle viscoelastic structures and reconstructed ice history for Antarctica from 1900 to 2020, which explain both the observed Global Navigation Satellite System crustal motions and Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment gravity changes in West Antarctica. This study demonstrates that a mantle rheology including a weak asthenosphere and temperature-dependent viscosity is consistent with both mantle convection at million-year timescales and ongoing decadal GIA occurring in West Antarctica.

more.title: Direct monitoring of breaching in deltaic submarine landslides
more.abstract: Submarine landslides threaten seabed infrastructure and trigger the transport of globally important amounts of sediment, carbon, and pollutants to deep-sea environments. However, fully submarine landslides have never been directly monitored in nature. Past hypotheses for their failure mechanism and dynamics therefore remain unvalidated for natural settings, including that prolonged upslope-migrating failures (breaching) occur in sandy seafloor environments. In this work, we present direct underwater monitoring of fully submarine landslides at Homathko Delta in western Canada that retrogress slowly upslope, indicating breaching-type failure. Their prolonged rather than instantaneous nature has important implications for the stress that seabed structures must be designed to withstand. Prolonged landslides also initiate sustained sediment flows (turbidity currents) that efficiently transport sediment, carbon, and pollutants further offshore.

more.title: Recent applications of asymmetric hydrogenation in total synthesis of natural products and drugs
more.abstract: Natural products with unique structures and promising bioactivities are vital for drug discovery. The efficient and concise synthesis of these natural products and analogues thus becomes even more critical for further drug screening. Over the past several decades, asymmetric hydrogenation has witnessed remarkable progress and evolved into a powerful and versatile strategy for the construction of chiral molecules. Starting from readily available building blocks, the enantioselective asymmetric hydrogenation of unsaturated bonds offers a straightforward strategy for the rapid construction of isolated or contiguous stereogenic centers at both early and late stages. In this review, we present a comprehensive overview of asymmetric hydrogenation of diverse unsaturated bonds, categorized by structural types. In particular, we highlight the application of asymmetric hydrogenation strategies in the total synthesis of natural products and drugs.

Additionally, by highlighting direct comparisons between reaction conditions in and out of solution, this review will underline key connections across synthetic methods and may serve as a guide in the selection of appropriate chemical and mechanical factors for initial precursor and COF screenings. Ultimately, the literature highlighted in this review will lower the barrier of entry, facilitating efficient design of mechanochemical syntheses for imine-derived COFs from the linkage up.

more.title: 5-Hydroxy-2(5 H )-furanone (HFO) – a versatile and bio-based platform chemical
more.abstract: )-furanone (5-hydroxybutenolide, HFO), a chiral maleic anhydride analogue, as a promising yet underexplored bio-based platform chemical. It critically assesses its synthetic accessibility from renewable furanic feedstocks and examines key transformation strategies that enable the generation of structurally diverse and enantioenriched derivatives. Emphasis is placed on its multifunctional reactivity, which underpins its application as versatile building block in asymmetric synthesis, fine chemicals, and materials science. Additionally, its potential as a precursor to industrially relevant C4 compounds under mild and sustainable conditions is evaluated. Its broader sustainability and industrial profile are also considered, including renewability, process efficiency, scalability, techno-economic considerations, and commercial relevance. Overall, this review demonstrates HFO not merely as another bio-based intermediate but positions it as strategically valuable platform molecule whose multifunctionality, accessibility, and adaptability enable innovative chemical design. Consequently, it represents a compelling candidate for bridging the gap between renewable resources and high-value applications, supporting the development of a more sustainable and forward-looking chemical industry.

more.title: Colloquium : Isotopes for medicine and fundamental physics
more.abstract: Isotopes, variants of elements distinguished by their neutron number, have important applications for medicine and fundamental science. This review explores the historical challenges and new technologies for enriching and detecting isotopes. We motivate the work by challenges posed by three of history’s greatest scientists: James Clerk Maxwell’s thought experiment on thermodynamics, Ernest Rutherford’s practical dilemma in radiochemistry, and Albert Einstein’s questions about the probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics. The journey to meet these challenges has catalyzed the development of innovative techniques for isotope separation. These advancements can mitigate the worldwide crisis in the supply of enriched isotopes. We then explore the expected impact of these new technologies on medicine, which include radioisotopes for cancer therapy and stable isotopes as tracers for metabolism. We explain the importance of developing scalable techniques for isotope detection and how it can help with early detection of certain diseases. Finally, we turn to basic science, outlining proposed new tests of quantum mechanics that utilize radioactive atomic clocks to probe the fundamental nature of determinism and distinguishability of atoms.

more.title: The Consequences of Pay Standing under Pay Range Transparency
more.abstract: Pay range transparency—that is, disclosing the minimum and maximum pay for a job rather than individuals’ actual pay—has become the most prevalent form of pay transparency. Yet, existing theories explain employee reactions to pay information through present-focused, interpersonal comparisons with coworkers’ pay. We theorize that pay range transparency instead directs employees to interpret their structural pay standing—their pay position relative to the disclosed range boundaries—as a forward-looking signal of the organization’s recognition and structural room for pay growth. Drawing on expectancy theory, we propose that structural pay standing has a curvilinear (attenuated-positive) effect on job satisfaction, intention to stay, and job performance, mediated by pay growth uncertainty: pay near the range minimum offers weak evidence that contributions will be recognized, whereas pay near the maximum reveals limited structural room for further growth, a pattern we term a ceiling effect. Pay-related procedural justice attenuates these effects. Four studies—a natural experiment (n = 371), an online experiment (n = 603), a three-wave field study (n = 525), and an experimental-causal-chain study (n = 392)—support our theorizing, establishing structural pay standing as distinct from interpersonal pay standing and revealing an unrecognized trade-off of pay range transparency.

more.title: Unramified Gromov–Witten and Gopakumar–Vafa invariants
more.journal: Journal of the American Mathematical Society
more.abstract: Kim, Kresch, and Oh defined unramified Gromov–Witten invariants. For threefolds, Pandharipande conjectured that these invariants are equal to the Gopakumar–Vafa invariants for Fano curve classes and primitive Calabi–Yau classes. We prove the conjecture using a wall-crossing method developed here. As a result, we obtain an algebro-geometric construction of Gopakumar–Vafa invariants in these cases.

more.title: Daddy’s Girl: Daughters, Managerial Decisions, and Gender Inequality
more.abstract: Using Danish registry data, we study how managers’ gender attitudes shape gender inequality in the workplace by exploiting the birth of a daughter—as opposed to a son—as a plausibly exogenous shock to male managers’ gender attitudes. Comparing within-firm changes in women’s labour outcomes depending on the gender of the manager’s newborn child, we find that women’s relative earnings and employment increase by 4.4% and 2.9%, respectively, following the birth of the manager’s first daughter. These effects are driven by an increase in managers’ propensity to substitute male hires with female hires that have comparable education, hours worked, and earnings. Consistent with this substitution channel, we do not detect any significant effect on firm performance. Because these effects emerge rapidly and persist over time, we can rule out the need for prolonged exposure to gender issues or for personal incentives tied to improving conditions for their own daughters as prerequisites for managers to promote gender equality within their firms.

more.title: Spatiotemporal intensity-cycling microscopy unveils many-body interactions and correlated transport in van der Waals semiconductors
Prospects of resolving and localising individual supermassive black hole binaries with pulsar timing arrays: the host ranking challenge
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: Pulsar Timing Arrays (PTAs) are soon expected to detect individually resolved supermassive black hole (SMBH) binaries, opening the possibility for multi-messenger discoveries. The biggest challenge will be to pinpoint the host galaxy in a large localisation area. We simulate realistic binary populations consistent with the gravitational wave (GW) background, projecting the PTA sensitivity for the next 0-10 years. We inject the loudest binary on top of the background and use a standard detection pipelines to constrain its properties. We cross-match the GW sky map with comprehensive all-sky galaxy catalogues and estimate the number of candidate hosts in the localisation area assessing, for the first time, the number of missing galaxies due to incomplete coverage. We develop a ranking system that excludes galaxies with properties inconsistent with the GW posteriors, and prioritizes the remaining galaxies for follow-up observations. We find a ≈21, ≈38 and ≈51 percent probability of resolving a binary in the next 0, 5 and 10 years, respectively, reduced to 0.3, 3.8 and 14.1 percent if we consider only sources potentially localisable within 2,000 deg2. The localisation areas span hundreds of square degrees, but shrink significantly with the addition of more data. They contain on average ≈190,000 early type galaxies and ≈40,000 active galactic nuclei, with ≈33,500 missing candidate hosts. Our ranking method can exclude about 37 percent of the potential hosts and efficiently rank those remaining when the galaxy catalogue provides SMBH masses and redshifts, but becomes more inefficient when it relies on apparent magnitudes.

more.title: Joint single-cell capture of Cas9 edits and transcriptomes reveals on- and off-target effects on gene expression
more.abstract: A longstanding barrier in genome engineering with CRISPR-Cas9 has been the inability to measure editing outcomes and their functional effects at single-cell resolution. Here we present Superb-seq, which captures single-cell edits and transcriptome effects by integrating Cas9 editing, T7 in situ transcription and single-cell RNA sequencing. We performed Superb-seq on 35,000 cells from three cell lines. Using seven guide RNAs to target four chromatin remodeler genes in 10,000 K562 cells, Superb-seq detected 5,761 edited cells, all on-target sites and 36 off-target sites. Superb-seq improved estimation of downstream perturbation effects on gene expression compared to Perturb-seq. We compared Superb-seq to 4 bulk off-target detection methods and identified between 6 and 210 edit sites across 3 benchmarking guides. Nineteen off-target edits were associated with differential gene expression, nine of which were cell type-specific. In summary, Superb-seq illuminates the consequences of Cas9 genome editing by connecting single-cell edits with changes in gene expression.

more.title: Spectroscopic Analysis of Fermi -detected Blazars using SDSS-V
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: The automated spectroscopic pipeline of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) systematically assigns Galactic star, galaxy, or typical quasar classifications to jet-dominated blazars, owing to the absence of a non-thermal jet continuum component in its template library. We present a physically motivated, multi-component spectral fitting pipeline applied to 746 optical counterparts of Fermi/4FGL-DR4 γ-ray sources in the SDSS-V Data Release 20 spectroscopic database, yielding 707 well-fitted blazar candidates dominated by Power-law+Galaxy (59.4%), Power-law+Lines (22.6%), and Power-law+QSO (15.0%) model families. WISE infrared (IR) photometry confirms that 85/88 sources originally misclassified as Galactic stars by SDSS have IR colours consistent with blazars, with 77 reclassified as BL Lacertae object (BL Lac) candidates. The pipeline naturally recovers the known cosmological separation between BL Lac and Flat Spectrum Radio Quasar (FSRQ) candidates and an order-of-magnitude difference in median γ-ray luminosity. Comparison with a validation sample of 111 sources in the Third Fermi-LAT Catalogue of High-Energy Sources (3FHL) yields a 10.4% reduction in catastrophic failures (η = 0.387 vs 0.432) over the SDSS pipeline. Equivalent width measurements confirm population-level consistency with the traditional |EW| = 5 Å classification boundary. However, 51.4% of individual BL Lac candidates show simultaneous emission and absorption features in single epoch spectra, pointing towards a more physically continuous description of blazar properties.

more.title: Bright Galaxies at Cosmic Dawn: A Cloud-Scale Star Formation Model Unifying Variable SFE, IMFs, and Stochasticity
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: To investigate the origins of the high abundance of UV-bright galaxies at z > 10, we present a new semi-analytic model that bridges the gap between small-scale star formation physics and large-scale galaxy evolution by explicitly tracking discrete star-forming clouds within smoothly evolving dark matter potentials. Unlike conventional semi-analytic models, our approach naturally captures the stochasticity of star formation, allowing us to isolate how cloud properties, star formation efficiencies (SFEs), and stellar initial mass functions (IMFs) shape the star-formation burstiness of early galaxies. Clouds are drawn sequentially from a cloud mass distribution, assigned an SFE and IMF depending on cloud mass, metallicity, and redshift, and evolve under the influence of short-timescale stellar feedback. We identify three distinct star formation regimes arising from the interplay between cloud masses, densities, and feedback timescales: a stochastic, feedback-limited regime in low-mass halos with long quiescent phases; a bursty regime regulated by the cloud mass distribution; and a smooth, continuous regime in massive halos. Our fiducial model adopts a dynamic IMF, an SFE linked to cloud properties and the IMF, and massive, moderately dense clouds. Varying assumptions reveals that top-heavy IMFs and enhanced SFEs in massive clouds amplify burstiness, while altering the upper cloud mass or density normalisation is secondary. Among model ingredients, the IMF most strongly impacts the UV luminosity function (LF), while switching to a constant SFE boosts the faint end, and reducing the maximum cloud mass decreases the bright end. These results demonstrate that cloud-scale physics critically shape early galaxy UV luminosity distributions.

more.title: Cubic-equivariant neural density functional theory for three-dimensional lattice fluids
more.abstract: We construct a neural classical density functional that acts directly on unrestricted three-dimensional density profiles. As a computationally tractable test bed, we consider parallel hard cubes of side length three on a simple cubic lattice. A fully convolutional network learns the one-body direct-correlation functional c ( 1 ) [ ρ ] from data obtained with grand-canonical Monte Carlo simulations in randomized external potentials. Complete profiles are used during both training and inference; a stochastic Bernoulli mask on the output sites makes full-profile training effective without explicitly extracting and storing overlapping local density windows. Averaging the first-layer kernels over all 48 rotations and reflections of the cubic point group additionally imposes exact cubic equivariance without data augmentation. We compare the learned functional with independent simulation data and with the lattice fundamental-measure functional of Lafuente and Cuesta. The neural functional markedly improves the homogeneous equation of state and the density profile at a planar hard wall. For the anisotropic pair distribution around a fixed particle, both functionals reproduce the principal packing shells, with their relative accuracy depending on lattice direction. These results demonstrate neural density-functional calculations on complete three-dimensional profiles while also identifying accurate full-dimensional training data, thermodynamic consistency, and structural correlations as the central challenges for extensions to continuum fluids.

more.title: Bound states in the continuum through quantum interference in ultracold atomic collisions
more.abstract: Quantum-mechanical interaction potentials support localized bound states below the dissociation threshold or delocalized scattering states above it. Although bound states are energetically isolated, scattering states couple a quantum system to environmental modes, making dissipation and loss intrinsic to open systems. Bound states in the continuum are an exception, as destructive interference keeps them localized within the scattering continuum. Theory predicts that such states can arise through interference between two Feshbach resonances coupled to a common continuum. Here we form such an interference-stabilized state in ultracold collisions of 6 Li atoms by coherently coupling two tunable Feshbach resonances using Floquet engineering. At a critical parameter point, elastic and inelastic coupling to the continuum vanish, producing a molecular state above the dissociation threshold. Consequently, resonant scattering features disappear and the colliding atoms become effectively transparent to one another. Full coupled-channel calculations and a minimal non-Hermitian model quantitatively reproduce our observations and identify the state as a Friedrich–Wintgen bound state in the continuum. These results show how quantum interference can control openness in quantum matter and enable the engineering of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians.

more.title: Formation of rotating supergiants via stellar mergers in dense clusters: Implications for black hole natal spins
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: We investigate how massive stellar mergers in young star clusters imprint on black hole spin distributions and the implications for gravitational wave sources. While mechanisms like hierarchical mergers and binary accretion can form rapidly spinning black holes, our central hypothesis is that angular momentum transferred during stellar mergers substantially affects the spins of the merger products and resulting black holes, with some merger products evolving into collapsar-like objects that retain thick accretion disks enabling efficient spin up. This is in contrast to the general expectation that black holes form with small spins, having shed most of their envelope angular momentum via winds and expansion before core collapse. Using roughly 150 N-body models generated with the Cluster Monte Carlo code, CMC, we analyze stellar mergers that lead to black hole formation, prioritizing “significant” events with mass ratio q > 0.1. After identifying optimal candidates, we explore stellar structure and post-merger evolution implications with MESA models to capture angular momentum injection and pre-collapse profiles most relevant for BH natal spin. In our current dataset representative of Milky Way-like globular clusters, up to roughly half of black holes are formed from such mergers, with roughly 10% from “significant” mergers. Angular momentum estimates indicate substantial spin-up during the merger, and trends with mass ratio and stellar properties suggest strong correlations with the final black hole spin. In some cases, dimensionless spin parameters of a ≃ 0.5 or more are expected. This process has important implications for the dynamical formation and retention of gravitational wave sources in clusters.

more.title: Echidna: a Bayesian framework for integrative inference of copy number alterations impacting phenotypic plasticity
more.abstract: The ability of cells to adapt their behavior in response to genetic or environmental changes is a fundamental biological process that drives cellular diversity in both normal and pathological contexts, including in tumor evolution. Copy number alterations (CNAs), which can include large-scale changes in genomic ploidy, play a key role in creating adaptive advantages in evolving cell populations. However, tracing these populations across experiments and disentangling the role of CNAs from other sources of transcriptional variability remains challenging and expensive. Here we present Echidna, a Bayesian hierarchical model that integrates single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk whole-genome sequencing data to enable robust integrative inference of CNAs, jointly across samples and treatment time points, to better understand the impact of genomic events on cellular phenotype. Applying Echidna to patient tumor specimens, we demonstrate its superior performance in clonal reconstruction and derive insights into therapy resistance mechanisms.

more.title: An open agentic AI co-scientist for clinical and biomedical discovery
more.abstract: Biomedical research is constrained by the time and domain expertise required to analyze increasingly large and complex datasets. Here we present OpenScientist, an open-source agentic AI co-scientist designed to address this gap by investigating scientist-defined queries and generating verifiable, data-grounded analyses. OpenScientist was evaluated by domain experts across five biomedical case studies, completing analyses in minutes that otherwise would take months of human time and expertise. It accurately quantified Alzheimer’s blood biomarker performance, generated a plasma proteomic survival model that predicted survival in a hidden-evaluation cohort, proposed a reproducible mechanism linking tau pathology to altered lysosomal acidification, generated multiple myeloma hypotheses validated in an external cohort with attenuated signal in randomized controls, and demonstrated concordance with an independent human analysis in a blinded, prespecified proteomic comparison. These results support the use of OpenScientist to assist biomedical data analysis in concert with human experts. To support research involving sensitive clinical datasets, OpenScientist can operate in a fully air-gapped environment using open-source models for inference. OpenScientist demonstrates that open, auditable, agentic AI can support real-world clinical research by researching the literature, generating hypotheses, executing analyses, and generating insights from complex datasets.

more.title: Integrated QTL mapping and CRISPR screening in pooled iPSC-derived microglia reveals genetic drivers of neurodegenerative risk
more.abstract: Mounting evidence implicates microglia in neurodegeneration, but linking disease-associated genetic variants to target genes and cellular phenotypes is hindered by the inaccessibility of these cells. We differentiated 261 human induced pluripotent stem cell lines into microglia-like (iMGL) cells in pools with phenotypic (differentiation, phagocytosis and migration) and single-cell transcriptomic readouts. Burden analysis of deleterious variants detected 36 genes influencing microglial phenotypes. Expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analysis identified 7,121 eQTL-associated genes and 79 colocalizations across four neurodegenerative disease genome-wide association studies, half of which had limited prior evidence of causality. Integration of eQTL and phenotypic associations highlighted the role of disease-relevant variants, including LRRK2 and TREM2 acting through microglial phagocytosis. A coupled CRISPR screen identified a role for TREM2 in phagocytosis and highlighted the importance of cell type in the directionality of phenotypic effects. By contextualizing variant effects within iMGLs in different inflammatory states, we provide a comprehensive framework for interpreting the function of risk loci in neurodegenerative disorders.

more.title: Piecewise Omnigenous Magnetohydrodynamic Equilibria as Fusion Reactor Candidates
more.abstract: In piecewise omnigenous magnetic fields, charged particles remain perfectly confined in the absence of collisions and turbulence. This concept extends the traditional notion of omnigenity, the theoretical principle upon which most of existing magnetic fusion reactor designs, including tokamaks, are based. While piecewise omnigenity broadens the range of potentially viable stellarator reactor candidates, it is achieved by relaxing the requirement of continuity in the magnetic-field strength, which could appear to pose significant challenges for the design of magnetohydrodynamic equilibria. In this work, a stellarator magnetic configuration is presented that satisfies the ideal magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium equation and that achieves unprecedented levels of piecewise omnigenity. As a result, it exhibits favorable transport characteristics, including reduced bulk radial (neoclassical and turbulent) transport, bootstrap current, and fast ion losses. In addition, the configuration displays robust magnetohydrodynamic stability across a range of β values and possesses a rotational transform profile compatible with an island divertor. Collectively, these features satisfy the standard set of physics criteria required for a viable reactor candidate which, until now, were believed to be attainable only by certain types of omnigenous stellarators.

shortlist.title: Union3.1: Reducing Systematics in Supernova Cosmology with Self-consistent Measurements of Host Galaxy Properties for 2000 Type Ia Supernovae
shortlist.abstract: Photometrically derived distances of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) rely on a ∼5% empirical correction based on host galaxy properties, e.g., global stellar mass. Unbiased cosmology inference therefore requires the self-consistent determination of host properties across the full range of redshifts probed, which we undertake here for approximately 2000 SNe in the Union3 compilation (now Union3.1). We use homogeneous optical-infrared photometry from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys to infer global galaxy properties using the stellar population synthesis and SED-fitting code Prospector . We find that the host masses of z < 0.10 SNe in Union3 were on average overestimated, while the opposite was true for z < 0.15 SNe in Pantheon+. After correction, the two studies’ average distance modulus estimated for low-redshift SNe, previously >0.03 mag discrepant, came into 0.01 mag agreement. Updating the UNITY supernova (SN) analysis, we find the uncertainties on all standardization parameters shrink to 0.6–0.9× their previous sizes. For flat Λ cold dark matter (CDM), we find from SNe alone Ω m = 0.34 4 − 0.025 + 0.026 (a −0.4 σ shift from Union3). We then combine with measurements of baryon acoustic oscillations and the cosmic microwave background exactly as done by DESI DR2 and find for flat w 0 w a CDM, w 0 = −0.719 ± 0.084 and w a = − 0.9 5 − 0.26 + 0.29 , corresponding to 3.4 σ evidence against a cosmological constant (down from 3.8 σ per DESI-DR2+Planck+Union3). shortlist.title: Evidence for hidden altermagnetism in Cs 1 − δ V 2 Te 2 O
shortlist.abstract: Altermagnets are characterized by anisotropic band/spin splittings in momentum space, dictated by their spin-space group symmetries. However, the real-space modulations of altermagnetism are often neglected and have not been explored experimentally. Here we combine neutron diffraction, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), spin-resolved ARPES and density functional theory to demonstrate that Cs_(1-δ)V₂Te₂O realizes a spatially modulated form of altermagnetism, i.e., hidden altermagnetism. Such a state in Cs_(1-δ)V₂Te₂O results from its G-type antiferromagnetism and two-dimensional electronic states, allowing for the development of spatially alternating altermagnetic layers, whose local spin polarizations are directly verified by spin-resolved ARPES measurements. Our experimental discovery of hidden altermagnetism broadens the scope of unconventional magnetism and opens routes to exploring emergent phenomena from real-space modulations of altermagnetic order.

shortlist.title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
shortlist.abstract: Large and giant double-stranded DNA viruses substantially affect eukaryotic ecology and evolution 1–4 . They prevail in the environment but are rarely found in the digestive system of animals 5,6 . Here we present the discovery of a diversified group of DNA viruses with large linear genomes, dubbed egoviruses, that comprise a putative viral order most closely related to animal-infecting poxviruses. Egoviruses are found worldwide, almost exclusively in the digestive system of humans, livestock and wild animals. The most prevalent human-specific egovirus is spread across continents, demonstrating a long-term association between egoviruses and the human gut microbiome. Eukaryotic homologues of egovirus core genes suggest that these viruses primarily infect Trichostomatia (ciliates), which assist ruminant digestive processes 7 , and Parabasalia (Metamonada), which influence animal immunity and gut microbiome ecology 8 . Egoviruses also contributed to the genetic makeup of polintons, endogenous viruses that proliferated in genomes of Trichomonas vaginalis 9 and its close Parabasalia relatives. Unlike poxviruses that form brick-shaped virions, egoviruses are predicted to form multilayered icosahedral capsids resembling those of asfuviruses and probably representing the ancestral virion structure. Egoviruses are the only known clade of double-stranded DNA viruses of eukaryotes prevailing in the animal digestive system. Phylogenomic analysis suggests an evolutionary scenario whereby egovirus-like ancestors of poxviruses infected anaerobic unicellular eukaryotes inside the gut of ancestral animals, before transitioning to animal cell infection, which was accompanied by the virion metamorphosis.

shortlist.title: Noise-Driven Odd Elastic Waves in Living Chiral Active Matter
shortlist.abstract: Chiral active matter is predicted to exhibit odd elasticity, with nontraditional elastic response arising from a combination of chirality, being out of equilibrium, and the presence of nonreciprocal interactions. One of the resulting phenomena is the possible occurrence of odd elastic waves in overdamped systems, although its experimental realization still remains elusive. Here we show that in overdamped active systems, noise is required to generate persistent elastic waves. In the chiral crystalline phase of active matter, such as that found recently in populations of swimming starfish embryos, the noise arises from the self-driving of active particles and their mutual collisions, a key factor that has been missing in previous studies. We identify the criterion for the occurrence of noise-driven odd elastic waves and construct the corresponding phase diagram, which is also applicable to general chiral active crystals. Our results can be used to predict the experimental conditions for achieving a transition to self-sustained elastic waves in overdamped active systems.

shortlist.title: First Indication of Low-Energy Solar Neutrino-Electron Scattering with PandaX-4T Run 2 Data
shortlist.abstract: We report a search for the solar proton–proton ( p p ) neutrino flux via neutrino–electron elastic scattering using the PandaX-4T Run 2 data set collected between 2024 and 2026, corresponding to an exposure of 1.9 tonne ⋅ yr. Before Run 2 data taking, the detector underwent a series of upgrades to improve its response and background conditions. Time variations of radioactive noble-gas impurities are constrained using the physics data themselves, complemented by measurements from the gas-assay system. The analysis introduced improvements in the data processing chain, detector response characterization, and background models. A blind spectral analysis was then performed on the electronic-recoil data across a wide energy range from 20 to 1000 keV. In combination with the Run 0 data published earlier, the pp neutrino flux is derived to be ( 8.5 ± 3.5 ) × 10 10 c m − 2 s − 1 , consistent with the prediction of the Standard Solar Model. The combined dataset yields a 2.2 σ statistical significance for solar neutrino-electron scattering, representing the first positive indication obtained using data below the Borexino analysis threshold of 165~keV.

shortlist.title: Mind the gap: Anti-critical quantum metrology
shortlist.abstract: Critical quantum metrology exploits the dramatic growth of the quantum Fisher information near quantum phase transitions to enhance the precision of parameter estimation. This enhancement is commonly associated with a closing energy gap, which causes the characteristic timescales for adiabatic preparation or relaxation to diverge with increasing system size. As a consequence, the apparent growth of the quantum Fisher information largely reflects the increasing evolution time induced by critical slowing down rather than a genuine improvement in metrological performance, thereby limiting the practical usefulness of such protocols. Here we show that the relationship between energy gaps, quantum correlations, and achievable precision in interacting quantum systems can be far more subtle. In particular, quantum-enhanced sensitivity can also emerge when the energy gap increases, eliminating critical slowing down and enabling substantially faster relaxation dynamics. Although the corresponding quantum Fisher information may decrease due to the shorter evolution time, the resulting precision can nevertheless remain quantum-enhanced. Building on this insight, we introduce an anti-critical quantum metrology scheme in which quantum-enhanced precision arises while the energy gap grows. We illustrate this mechanism using the quantum Rabi model, thereby identifying a route to metrological advantage that avoids the slow dynamics associated with conventional criticality.

shortlist.title: Deciphering the Physical Origin of GRB 240825A: A Long Gamma-Ray Burst Lacking a Bright Supernova
shortlist.abstract: We present a comprehensive multiwavelength analysis of GRB 240825A, a bright gamma-ray burst (GRB) detected by Fermi and Swift, with a prompt duration ( T 90 ∼ 4 s in the 50–300 keV band measured by the Gamma-ray Burst Monitor) near the boundary separating short and long GRBs, prompting a detailed investigation into its classification and progenitor. We use classical prompt metrics (duration, minimum variability timescale, lag, and spectral hardness) and modern classification techniques (machine learning–based t-SNE, support vector machine, energy- hardness duration, and ε ≡ E γ , iso , 52 / E p , z , 2 5 / 3 ) and find most properties (prompt energetics, placement on the Amati relation, and spectral lag) of GRB 240825A consistent with a collapsar origin. However, extensive late-time optical and near-infrared follow-up with the 10.4 m Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC) telescope and the 8.4 m Large Binocular Telescope reveals no bright supernova (SN; like SN 1998bw) is detected down to stringent limits (e.g., m r > 25.0 mag at 17.59 days), despite a redshift of z = 0.659 measured from GTC spectroscopy. Host-galaxy spectral energy distribution modeling with Prospector indicates a massive, star-forming galaxy typical of collapsar GRB hosts, though with a large offset. We compare these findings with hybrid events like GRB 211211A, GRB 230307A, GRB 200826A, including supernovae-GRBs, and conclude that GRB 240825A most likely originated from a massive star collapse, possibly with the associated AN heavily obscured or intrinsically faint. This study emphasizes the need for multiwavelength follow-up and a multilayered classification to determine GRB progenitors.
