fundamentals.title: Uncovering internal sensory evidence reveals the nature of confidence computation in multi-alternative perceptual decision making.
fundamentals.abstract: A central goal of perceptual decision making is to determine the computations underlying choice and confidence in complex, multi-alternative tasks. However, revealing these computations requires knowledge of the internal sensory evidence upon which the computations operate. Unfortunately, unlike for two-choice tasks, there is no established method in multi-alternative tasks to determine how stimuli are transformed into internal sensory evidence. Here we address this critical gap by developing a novel modeling paradigm that reveals how the brain transforms external stimuli into internal sensory evidence during multi-alternative decision making in the context of numerosity tasks. Across three experiments that feature two-, three-, and five-choice conditions, we show that the internal sensory evidence in our numerosity task can be described with a simple, two-parameter equation that fits data for up to 12 conditions. Critically, the ability to model the internal sensory evidence allowed us to test six theories of confidence computation. Our results support a model where confidence reflects the raw evidence difference between the top two alternatives. These results establish a new numerosity paradigm in which a two-parameter equation can be used to determine the internal sensory evidence for a potentially unlimited number of multi-alternative conditions and reveal the confidence computation in multi-alternative tasks. fundamentals.title: Named Reactions under Mechanochemical Conditions: A Critical Survey
fundamentals.abstract: Mechanochemistry has progressed from a niche interest to a core method for solvent-free synthesis, providing sustainable and mechanistically unique alternatives to traditional solution-based chemistry. When controlled impact, shear, or vibrational energy is applied under solvent-free or solvent-lean conditions, reactions are promoted within dynamically renewed interfacial regions, revealing new patterns of selectivity, energy efficiency, and process design. This review surveys the historical development, fundamental principles, and analytical frameworks of mechanochemistry, together with an extensive compilation of named organic reactions conducted under mechanochemical conditions. By comparing mechanochemical reactions with their solution-phase counterparts, this review clarifies how stress-induced activation, microsolvation (η control), and auxiliary-mediated interfaces influence reaction kinetics, selectivity, and scalability. Emerging platforms, such as twin-screw extrusion (TSE), resonant acoustic mixing (RAM), and bead mills, extend these advantages toward scale-up and, in the case of TSE, continuous manufacturing, bridging laboratory-scale discoveries and industrial applications. Mechanochemistry functions both as a practical enabling platform and as a conceptual framework for Green Chemistry, embracing atom economy, solvent reduction, and operational safety within a unified solid-state synthetic framework.

fundamentals.title: When AUC Meets Generative Reconstruction: A Unified Principle for Balanced Visual Representation Learning
fundamentals.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
fundamentals.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) require visual encoders that extract fine-grained visual features while constructing semantically disentangled and discriminative representations. Conventional methodologies encounter a fundamental trade-off: contrastive learning enhances inter-class discrimination by suppressing intra-class variability, whereas generative reconstruction emphasizes perceptual fidelity but lacks explicit comparative supervision. The naive aggregation of these objectives via composite loss functions often induces optimization conflicts and instability due to gradient interference within the shared latent space. To resolve this, we introduce a unified representation-learning paradigm that reformulates generative reconstruction as a discriminative ranking problem within the generative output manifold. Our approach maintains perceptual reconstruction as a supervisory signal and integrates a ranking-based discriminative constraint by systematically ordering matched and mismatched reconstruction outputs. This formulation embeds discriminative information seamlessly into the generative process, alleviating the risk of loss competition. Specifically, we propose AUC Generative Reconstruction (AUCGR), which optimizes the area under the ROC curve (AUC) by ensuring higher scores for matched pairs than for mismatched pairs, and Partial AUC Generative Reconstruction (pAUCGR), which addresses supervision bias by focusing on mismatched comparisons within reliable feature subspaces. The proposed objectives are designed to be plug-and-play, requiring no architectural modifications to existing generative reconstruction frameworks. Theoretical analysis establishes rigorous connections to AUC/pAUC optimization and provides generalization guarantees. Extensive…

fundamentals.title: Constructive Ordinal Exponentiation
fundamentals.abstract: In classical mathematics, ordinal arithmetic is well-studied; constructively, addition and multiplication are well-known. We study constructive ordinal exponentiation, where ordinals are taken to be transitive, extensional, and wellfounded orders on sets. We present a negative result showing that general constructive ordinal exponentiation is impossible, but we suggest two definitions that come close. The first definition is abstract and solely motivated by the expected equations; this works as long as the base of the exponential is positive. The second definition is based on decreasing lists and can be seen as a constructive version of Sierpiński’s definition via functions with finite support; this requires the base to have a trichotomous least element. Whenever it makes sense to ask the question, the two constructions are equivalent, allowing us to prove algebraic laws, cancellation properties, and preservation of decidability of the exponential. The core ideas do not depend on any specific constructive set theory or type theory, but a concrete computer-checked mechanization using the Agda proof assistant is given in homotopy type theory.

fundamentals.title: Differentiable Programming for Differential Equations: A Review
fundamentals.abstract: The differentiable programming paradigm is a cornerstone of modern scientific computing. It refers to numerical methods for computing the gradient of a numerical model’s output. Many scientific models are based on differential equations, in which differentiable programming plays a crucial role in calculating model sensitivities, inverting model parameters, and training hybrid models that combine differential equations with data-driven approaches. Furthermore, recognizing the strong synergies between inverse methods and machine learning offers the opportunity to establish a coherent framework applicable to both fields. Differentiating functions based on the numerical solution of differential equations is nontrivial. Numerous methods based on a wide variety of paradigms have been proposed in the literature, each with pros and cons specific to the type of problem investigated. Here, we provide a comprehensive review of existing techniques to compute derivatives of numerical solutions of differential equations. We first discuss the importance of gradients of solutions of differential equations in a variety of scientific domains. Second, we lay out and compare the mathematical foundations of the various approaches. Third, we cover computational considerations and explore the solutions available in modern scientific software. Last but not least, we provide best practices and recommendations for practitioners. We hope that this work accelerates the fusion of scientific models and data and fosters a modern approach to scientific modeling.

fundamentals.title: Metal-Centered Spin-State Switching Promotes Stereodivergent Synthesis of E - and Z -Allylamines
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
fundamentals.abstract: Spin state offers a fundamental yet underexplored handle for controlling stereoselectivity in transition-metal catalysis. Here we show that metal-centered spin-state switching, within an invariant weak-field bipyridine framework, promotes E/Z divergence in allylic substitution, enabling access to geometrically defined allylamines from common precursors. High-spin Ni catalysts selectively afford E-allylamines, whereas low-spin Pd catalysts deliver the corresponding Z-isomers. Broad metal studies with Fe, Rh and Ir systems further support the association between metal-centered spin state and alkene geometry. Mechanistic experiments and density functional theory (DFT) analyses reveal the origin of this stereodivergent outcome: spin-state-dependent electronic structures reshape catalyst–substrate interactions, thereby selectively stabilizing the competing E- or Z-forming transition states. The paired E/Z products enable concise syntheses of pharmaceutically relevant molecules and reveal configuration-dependent biological activities. This work establishes catalyst spin state as a design parameter for the stereodivergent control of alkene geometry.

fundamentals.title: First-principles Turbulence-driven Deflagration-to-detonation Transition Mechanism for Near-Chandrasekhar-mass White Dwarf Progenitors
fundamentals.abstract: Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) play an important role throughout astrophysics, most notably as standardizable cosmological candles. Yet, their stellar progenitors and explosion mechanism remain areas of active investigation. For decades, the canonical model for normal brightness SNe Ia used in cosmology was a carbon–oxygen white dwarf (WD) approaching the Chandrasekhar mass ( M Ch ) as it accretes from a nondegenerate stellar companion. Previously, all models of near- M Ch SNe Ia invoked an ad hoc assumption on the critical process of detonation initiation, and could therefore be tuned to a variety of outcomes. Here, we present global 3D hydrodynamical simulations of near- M Ch progenitors, which incorporate, for the first time, a laboratory-validated ab initio mechanism for the turbulence-driven deflagration-to-detonation transition (tDDT) based on the Chapman–Jouguet deflagration criterion. The tDDT mechanism is highly efficient, leading to detonation initiation, which is prompt in comparison to most prior work. Despite spanning a factor of 6 in central ignition density and a range of qualitatively distinct ignition topologies, all models converge on nearly identical synthetic spectra at peak luminosity, spectroscopically matched to the overluminous SN 1999aa. The tDDT mechanism drives each progenitor to a common detonation configuration from diverse initial conditions, providing a physical foundation for the ignition-insensitive detonation outcomes implicit in the empirical standardizability of SNe Ia. This provides the first physically motivated, self-consistent pathway for delayed detonation in SN Ia simulations. Further work is necessary to understand how this mechanism might produce more delayed detonation initiation and potentially fail, thereby yielding Type Iax…

fundamentals.title: Local interactions drive hyperuniform tissue coverage during development
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: In living tissues, branched cells must efficiently cover territories to perform essential functions ranging from neural signaling to immune surveillance. However, how cells collectively establish and optimize tissue-scale coverage without global regulation remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a biophysical theory of interacting branched cells and show that coupling their growth to neighbor repulsion drives efficient tissue tiling with minimal territorial overlap. Strikingly, our model predicts that the same local mechanism progressively suppresses long-range density fluctuations during development, driving the system toward a large-scale order called hyperuniformity. We confirm these theoretical predictions on microglial patterning in the developing retina and show that in perturbation experiments with limited arbor growth, both tiling and fluctuation suppression are disrupted. Our results reveal that two seemingly distinct features of tissue organization, efficient space-filling and large-scale order, share a single dynamical origin, suggesting a general principle for robust tissue patterning.

fundamentals.title: Linear scaling reveals low-dimensional structure in observable microbial dynamics
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: Microbial communities often exhibit apparently complex dynamics driven by myriad interactions among community members and with their environments. Yet, practical modeling and control are often based on a limited number of observables, raising fundamental questions: are these observed dynamics low-dimensional? If so, how does the low dimensionality enable predictions with limited information? Here, we report an emergent simplicity that the temporal dynamics of observable microbial populations can be captured by low-dimensional representations. Using variational autoencoders, we define a critical latent dimension ( E c ) that operationally quantifies the smallest latent dimension required for high-fidelity reconstruction of observable microbial dynamics under a specified criterion. Despite the complexity of unobserved background dynamics, we find E c to be drastically lower than the community’s apparent degrees of freedom. E c scales linearly with the number of observables, providing an empirical principle for determining representation complexity. This principle holds across simulations of pairwise interacting communities, consumer–resource dynamics, spatially distributed microbial patches, and plasmid transfer, experiments with engineered and environment-derived communities, and human microbiomes. Our findings establish a scaling law for microbial community dynamics and demonstrate that low-dimensional representations of observable dynamics retain information useful for selected prediction tasks without direct measurement of the complete community.

fundamentals.title: Curvature-guided chiral collective organization of myoblast tissues
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: Surface curvature is a fundamental geometric cue in tissue morphogenesis, yet its role in guiding collective cell organization has remained elusive. Here, we show that curvature acts as a geometric control parameter that shapes supracellular alignment and chirality while modulating myogenic differentiation in myoblast tissues. Cells cultured on curved substrates self-organize into robust helical assemblies whose handedness is set, and can be reversed, by the sign of curvature: convex fibers produce right-handed helices, whereas concave channels invert the chirality. We identify a clockwise bias in single-cell motion associated with the helical actin cytoskeleton. A minimal continuum theory coupling an effective chiral drive to curvature quantitatively captures the emergence and reversal of tissue-scale chiral alignment. On substrates with spatially varying curvature, local curvature gradients organize patterned multicellular architectures while preserving a global handedness. Curvature is also associated with myogenic state, with higher curvature linked to reduced or delayed differentiation. Together, these findings reveal how complex geometries shape the alignment, symmetry, and cellular state of living tissues.

fundamentals.title: Foiling Black Hole Foils: Revealing Horizon Alternatives with Baryonic Atmospheres
fundamentals.abstract: Event horizons are a defining feature of black holes. Consequently, there have been many efforts to probe their existence in astrophysical black hole candidates, spanning 10 orders of magnitude in mass. Nevertheless, horizons remain an obstacle to unifying general relativity and quantum mechanics, most sharply presented by the information paradox. This has motivated a proliferation of horizonless alternatives (black hole foils) that avoid event horizons and are therefore presumably benign. We explore the fate of accreting material in the context of spherically symmetric horizonless compact objects in the steady state regime. We find that for typical accreting astronomical targets, foils can develop an optically thick, convectively stable baryonic atmosphere, immediately implying the creation of an emitting photosphere at modest redshift even when the surface redshift is extreme. The emergent photosphere luminosity is driven toward the accretion powered equilibrium value and is only weakly sensitive to the foil redshift. Moreover, local gas–surface interaction provides a microphysical lower bound on the effective base temperature, insulating the atmosphere from arbitrarily cold foils. The unknown properties of the foil enter only through local boundary conditions controlling baryon processing and thermal coupling at the surface, making the solutions broadly applicable to horizonless alternatives that do not invoke significant additional nonlocal interactions. Thus, under minimal assumptions (GR exterior and local surface interactions), spherically symmetric horizonless foils in accreting systems are generically observationally exposed: the absence of a thermal photosphere directly constrains or rules out broad classes of such models.

fundamentals.title: Evolution, information content, and optimality of gene regulatory architectures
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: Evolution of genetic regulatory sequences is shaped by their genotype-phenotype map, but this map itself can evolve via changes in the molecular machinery that reads out the regulatory sequences. Using population genetics theory, we derive a maximization principle, which implies that genotype-phenotype maps will evolve to associate fit phenotypes with larger numbers of possible genotypes. Mathematically, this builds on analogies between population genetics and statistical physics, as well as optimal coding in information theory. The results are particularly interesting in the context of transcriptional regulation, where optimal values of certain parameters that determine the gene regulatory architecture can be derived even without a complete knowledge of the molecular mechanisms involved. We illustrate the theory using a simplified model of transcription factor (TF) binding to cis-regulatory elements (CREs): the fraction of possible CREs across the entire genotype space that bind a given TF evolves to match the fraction of CREs under selection to bind that TF. Similar "frequency matching" results are expected to emerge generically, because selection implicitly moves the entire regulatory architecture toward a fitness maximum, determining the "replicated genotype-phenotype map" for all CREs, while it simultaneously adapts toward individually fit CREs on that map. We discuss the subtleties and limitations of the theory related to biophysical constraints and the need for mutational robustness. Last, our theory suggests a possible mathematical definition for evolvability with predictive power that can be tested in evolutionary simulations and, ultimately, in comparative genetics studies.

fundamentals.title: Self-Induced Spin Glass in Triangular-Lattice MnNCN Stabilized by High-Pressure Synthesis
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
fundamentals.abstract: The realization of spin glasses in the absence of structural disorder remains an enduring challenge in condensed matter physics and solid-state chemistry. Geometrical frustration provides a route to disordered magnetism in long-range ordered crystals, yet canonical self-induced spin glass (SISG) beyond ultrapure rare-earth elements remains experimentally elusive. Here, we realize a metastable transition-metal SISG phase in MnNCN (R3̅m) via high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) synthesis, stabilizing a nonequilibrium state with enhanced magnetic competition. Magnetic measurements establish canonical spin-glass behavior, featuring a freezing temperature of 38.15 K and characteristic slowing-down dynamics, alongside a high coercivity of 1838 Oe. First-principles calculations reveal this SISG behavior is inherently rooted in the frustrated Mn triangular lattice. Mapping the energetic hierarchy uncovers strong competition among distinct antiferromagnetic superexchange pathways. Crucially, high-pressure-driven anisotropic lattice compression alters the Mn-ligand orbital overlap, significantly amplifying the intralayer coupling within the ab triangular planes. This chemical–mechanical modulation intensifies the competition between intralayer and dominant interlayer couplings, producing a strongly frustrated three-dimensional magnetic network. Energy evaluations verify a profound near-degeneracy among these competing states. Rapid quenching kinetically preserves this structurally ordered metastable phase, generating the complex energy landscape characteristic of a spin glass. Electronic-structure analyses further identify the Mn–N–C–N–Mn superexchange pathway mediated by covalent [N═C═N]2– ligands as the origin of magnetic coupling, yielding an intrinsic phase robustness…

fundamentals.title: Diffusion Models for Small-Molecule Design
fundamentals.abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have emerged as a class of generative models for controllable small-molecule design in drug discovery capable of progressively transforming noisy or partially specified molecular states into candidate structures under structural, geometric, and property constraints. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of the methodological foundations and representative applications of diffusion-based molecular generation, emphasizing the alignment among molecular representations, generative dynamics, controllable design, and evaluation and validation. Particular attention is given to recent advances in property- and structure-guided generation, target-aware and fragment-based design, multiobjective optimization, and synthesis-aware generation. We also discuss the roles of data sets, computational evaluation, and prospective experiments in assessing the chemical and biological relevance of generated molecules. By organizing these developments within a unified conceptual framework, we provide computational chemists and drug discovery researchers with a structured roadmap that balances the mathematical rigor with chemical intuition. Throughout, we highlight current methodological limitations and unresolved challenges and conclude with future directions toward chemically credible and experimentally grounded molecular design. To facilitate navigation of this rapidly evolving field, we introduce an interactive companion platform (https://diffsmd.scbdd.com) that provides a curated, continuously updated repository of model architectures and visualizations.

fundamentals.title: Bright Galaxies at Cosmic Dawn: A Cloud-Scale Star Formation Model Unifying Variable SFE, IMFs, and Stochasticity
fundamentals.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
fundamentals.abstract: To investigate the origins of the high abundance of UV-bright galaxies at z > 10, we present a new semi-analytic model that bridges the gap between small-scale star formation physics and large-scale galaxy evolution by explicitly tracking discrete star-forming clouds within smoothly evolving dark matter potentials. Unlike conventional semi-analytic models, our approach naturally captures the stochasticity of star formation, allowing us to isolate how cloud properties, star formation efficiencies (SFEs), and stellar initial mass functions (IMFs) shape the star-formation burstiness of early galaxies. Clouds are drawn sequentially from a cloud mass distribution, assigned an SFE and IMF depending on cloud mass, metallicity, and redshift, and evolve under the influence of short-timescale stellar feedback. We identify three distinct star formation regimes arising from the interplay between cloud masses, densities, and feedback timescales: a stochastic, feedback-limited regime in low-mass halos with long quiescent phases; a bursty regime regulated by the cloud mass distribution; and a smooth, continuous regime in massive halos. Our fiducial model adopts a dynamic IMF, an SFE linked to cloud properties and the IMF, and massive, moderately dense clouds. Varying assumptions reveals that top-heavy IMFs and enhanced SFEs in massive clouds amplify burstiness, while altering the upper cloud mass or density normalisation is secondary. Among model ingredients, the IMF most strongly impacts the UV luminosity function (LF), while switching to a constant SFE boosts the faint end, and reducing the maximum cloud mass decreases the bright end. These results demonstrate that cloud-scale physics critically shape early galaxy UV luminosity distributions.

fundamentals.title: De Novo Folding Mechanisms of Lasso Peptides
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
fundamentals.abstract: Lasso peptides adopt a distinctive [1] rotaxane conformation, yet the principles governing the folding of this kinetically trapped structure have remained elusive. Here, we integrated extensive molecular dynamics simulations and deep learning to elucidate the de novo folding mechanism of 20 lasso peptides lacking secondary post-translational modifications. We constructed Multi-Ensemble Markov Models for each lasso peptide and uncovered a consistent uphill folding landscape with spontaneous folding probabilities below 0.8%. Loop stability strongly correlated with folding propensity. Both simulations and experiments suggested that enhancing loop β-hairpin formation promotes folding of microcin J25, the well-studied lasso peptide extensively characterized as an in vitro model. This was confirmed by in silico loop-swap chimeras: grafting the microcin J25 loop onto the structurally similar klebsidin conferred prefolded stability. Leveraging Variational AutoEncoder-based pathway clustering, we resolved distinct pathway channels and representative folding pathways, further supporting this conclusion from a kinetic perspective. Additionally, a substantial entropy penalty was found to oppose lasso peptide folding. Simulations mimicking enzymatic spatial confinement reduced this penalty and stabilized the prefolded state. Together, these findings establish representative folding models and fundamental thermodynamic and kinetic principles which may be applied toward the rational engineering of lasso peptides.

food.title: Prevalence and levels of mycotoxins in poultry feed and ingredients: a global systematic review and meta-analysis
food.abstract: Mycotoxins are a global concern due to their widespread occurrence throughout the food chain and their potential risks to human and animal health. This study investigated the global prevalence and concentrations of mycotoxins in poultry feed and its components, assessing their potential health implication. Following the PRISMA methodology, 78 articles were included, with data processed (outlier removal) and analysed using STATA®. Globally, fumonisins B1 (FB1) and B2 (FB2) were the most prevalent (70% and 68%), with concentrations of 1,159 µg kg –1 and 164 µg kg –1 , respectively. The prevalence of aflatoxins (AFs), zearalenone (ZEN), deoxynivalenol (DON), ochratoxins (OTs), T-2/HT-2 toxins, emerging (overall pooled value of fusaric acid (FUS), enniatins (ENNs), apicidin (API), alternariol (AOH), nivalenol (NIV), beauvericin (BEA), patulin (PAT), moniliformin (MON), diacetoxyscirpenol (DAS), ergot alkaloids (EA), kojic acid (KA), tenuazonic acid (TeA), scirpentriol (SCIRP), cyclopiazonic acid (CPA), citrinin (CIT), fusarenon-X (FUS-X), T-2 triol/tetraol, and sterigmatocystin (STG)), and masked/modified mycotoxins (overall pooled value of deoxynivalenol-3-glucoside (D3G), 3-acetyl-deoxynivalenol (3-Ac-DON), and 15-acetyl-deoxynivalenol (15-Ac-DON)) appeared as 64%, 59%, 46%, 41%, 45%, 53% and 37%, with corresponding concentrations of 25.2, 204, 522, 36.6, 154, 15.8 and 35.0 µg kg –1 , respectively. Cotton, barley, sunflower, and maize meals showed high concentrations of multiple mycotoxins ( viz ., ZEN, FBs, and DON). Except for the AFs, all concentrations were below the Maximum Limits (MLs)/Guidance Values (GVs) established by the European Commission (EC 2002; EC 2006). food.title: Genetic dissection of carcass composition and fat deposition traits in a Pekin duck × Liancheng White duck F₂ population using univariate and cross-trait GWAS
food.abstract: Single-trait and multi-trait genome-wide association studies (C-GWAS) were performed on 18 carcass- and growth-related traits in a Pekin duck × Liancheng White duck F₂ population (n = 242; slaughtered at 70 d) using 12.8 million SNPs. Single-trait GWAS identified major-effect loci for carcass weight and half-eviscerated weight on chromosome 2 (104.68 Mb), for leg muscle weight on chromosome 2 (57.91 Mb), and for abdominal fat weight and skin fat thickness on chromosome 3 (88.46 Mb), revealing heterogeneous genetic architectures ranging from major-effect variants to polygenic backgrounds; the broad signal intervals were consistent with long-range LD in the F₂ population. Multi-trait C-GWAS substantially improved detection power, identifying 79022 genome-wide significant SNPs (P < 5×10⁻⁸), of which 69.9% were located within gene regions-markedly higher than the genomic background (∼45%). Functional enrichment of the 7,889 annotated candidate genes highlighted cell adhesion, actin cytoskeleton organization, and focal adhesion as core biological themes, with the IgSF-CAM signaling pathway (apla04517, Padjust = 2.9×10⁻¹²) as the most significantly enriched KEGG pathway-a signal not detected in single-trait analyses. Tissue-specific eQTL colocalization identified liver (33471 pairs) and muscle (29426 pairs) as the primary effector tissues, with MLH3 showing pleiotropic signals across multiple tissues, NGEF exhibiting muscle-specific enrichment, and PINK1 dominant in liver. Integrating SNP annotation, functional enrichment, and eQTL colocalization, six high-confidence candidate genes (MLH3, NGEF, PINK1, PRDM16, PTK2, and CADM2) were prioritized. food.title: Plasma-based technologies for aquatic product preservation: Balancing microbial control and oxidative deterioration
food.abstract: : Background Aquatic products are highly nutritious but are particularly susceptible to microbial contamination, lipid oxidation, and protein degradation during postharvest handling and storage, posing challenges to food safety, quality preservation, and sustainable cold-chain logistics. Atmospheric cold plasma (ACP) and plasma-activated liquids (PALs), particularly plasma-activated water (PAW), have emerged as promising non-thermal preservation technologies because they generate reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) capable of inactivating microorganisms while minimizing thermal damage. Scope and approach This review critically summarizes recent advances in the application of ACP and PALs for aquatic product preservation, with particular emphasis on the mechanisms underlying microbial inactivation and the complex interactions among microorganisms, proteins, lipids, and plasma-generated reactive species. Rather than considering microbial safety and quality independently, this review highlights how ACP simultaneously regulates microbial growth, protein oxidation, lipid oxidation, and volatile flavor formation, thereby determining the overall preservation outcome. Key findings and conclusions Current evidence indicates that the efficacy of ACP is highly dependent on treatment intensity, plasma operating conditions, and food matrix characteristics, requiring a careful balance between effective microbial control and the prevention of excessive oxidative deterioration. The review further discusses key barriers to industrial implementation, including the lack of standardized processing protocols, insufficient dose–response characterization, limited toxicological evidence, equipment scalability, and regulatory uncertainty. food.title: Effects of different Eimeria maxima infection doses on growth performance and gut and bone health in a dual-infection model of necrotic enteritis in layer chicks
food.abstract: Necrotic enteritis (NE) is an enteric disease that causes approximately 6 billion USD in annual losses to the global poultry industry. Although NE has been extensively studied in broiler chickens, limited information is available regarding NE in layers. Therefore, this study evaluated the effects of different doses of E. maxima (EM) on growth performance, intestinal health, and bone parameters in a dual infection model of NE in layer chicks. A total of 300 twenty-one-day old Hy-Line W-36 pullet chicks were randomly allocated into five treatments with six replicates of 10 birds each: (1) NC, non-challenged control; (2) CP, Clostridium perfringens control; (3) EM10K+CP; (4) EM20K+CP; and (5) EM40K+CP. Birds in the EM10K+CP, EM20K+CP, and EM40K+CP groups received 10,000, 20,000, and 40,000 sporulated E. maxima oocysts respectively on 0 days post-inoculation (DPI), whereas the CP and all EM+CP groups received 1 × 10⁹ CFU of NetB+ C. perfringens strain Del-1 challenge on 4 and 5 DPI. Body weight (BW) was recorded on 4,7 and 14 DPI while feed intake (FI) was measured daily. Intestinal permeability at 6 and 9 DPI; intestinal lesions, C. perfringens counts, oocyst shedding, intestinal morphology, and gene expression were evaluated at 7 DPI. Body composition and tibial bone characteristics were assessed on 7 and 14 DPI. Data were analyzed using one-way ANOVA with Tukey's HSD test and orthogonal polynomial contrasts for linear and quadratic responses. During 0-7 DPI, EM40K+CP had reduced BWG and FI by 33.6% and 12.8%, respectively, and increased FCR by 32.2% compared with NC (linear, P < 0.001). food.title: The role of selenoprotein O in alleviating intestinal inflammation with nano-selenium: A perspective based on pyroptosis and macrophage polarization crosstalk
food.abstract: Terbuthylazine (Ter) can induce excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, triggering intestinal damage. During this pathological process, macrophages undergo M1 polarization to drive inflammatory progression. As a highly efficient Se source, Nano-selenium (Nano-Se) has been proven to possess excellent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory features. Therefore, this study aims to investigate whether Nano-Se alleviates Ter-induced intestinal injury and elucidate its specific mechanism. Broilers, CSIEC and HD11 cells were treated with Ter or/and Nano-Se. We also constructed a selenoprotein O (SelO) overexpression model in CSIEC and HD11 cells to explore the specific mechanism. Integrated network toxicology and bioinformatics analyses revealed the involvement of Ter in oxidative stress, macrophage polarization, metabolism, pyroptosis, and inflammation process. Experimental results found that Ter exposure promoted excessive ROS production, M1 macrophage polarization, glycolysis, pyroptosis and inflammation by suppressing SelO expression. Besides, M1 macrophage and CSIEC cells pyroptosis formed a vicious cycle that aggravated inflammatory responses under Ter stimulation. Notably, Nano-Se treatment reversed these results by modulating SelO. In summary, by combining network toxicology analysis with experimental results, research revealed that Nano-Se treatment could provide effective protection against Ter-induced intestinal inflammation in broilers. Overall, this study enriches the understanding of Se's biological functions, establishing a solid foundation for expanding its potential application values.

food.title: Essential oils in food preservation: Integrating antimicrobial efficacy with evolutionary and microbiome selectivity considerations
authors: Eliza de Jesus Barros dos Santos
food.abstract: Background Essential oils (EOs) and their constituents (EOCs) can support food preservation, but antimicrobial efficacy alone does not characterize every surviving-cell state or community response. Minimum inhibitory and bactericidal concentrations, colony-forming units, and shelf-life measurements remain essential; additional endpoints may be needed when exposure histories or non-target populations are relevant. Scope and approach This critical narrative review integrates foundational and recent studies on EO/EOC exposure, microbial stress responses, experimental evolution, loss of culturability, and food microbial communities. Evidence is distinguished by intervention, experimental system, exposure design, and endpoint. Laboratory and non-food findings are used for mechanistic context, with their transfer to foods explicitly limited. Key findings and conclusions Reported responses include injury, altered stress tolerance, stable resistance in selected experimental systems, cross-protection, collateral sensitivity, and viable but nonculturable (VBNC) states; other studies detected no increased tolerance under the conditions tested. Food studies also report community and metabolite changes, although relative-abundance profiles and associations seldom establish ecological causality. We propose an integrated, evolution-aware and microbiome-selective preservation perspective organized by the Microbial Fate Map, Sublethal EO Paradox, Microbiome Selectivity Index (MSI), and Evolutionary Safety Window (ESW). MSI and ESW are proposed conceptual frameworks, without validated scores or boundaries. Their value must be tested against conventional efficacy and quality endpoints in defined food systems. food.title: Hydrogen-dependent sulfur and iron reduction by marine thermophiles as analogs for early Earth and ocean world processes
food.abstract: Life on the early Earth was likely anaerobic, H 2 dependent, CO 2 fixing, and thermophilic in a marine hydrothermal setting. Geochemical and mineral evidence suggests that sulfur and iron respiration occurred during the Paleoarchean (3.6–3.2 Ga). However, the predominant mechanisms of H 2 -dependent sulfur and iron respiration in hydrothermal systems, then or now, have yet to be elucidated. Studying these processes in microorganisms from modern hydrothermal systems provides context for interpreting the characteristics of life during the Paleoarchaean. All the bacteria and archaea that have been cultured and characterized as extremely thermophilic, marine, H 2 dependent, and sulfur reducing or iron reducing (36 species) were surveyed for genes related to energy generation and terminal reduction processes. Respiratory hydrogenases, Nuo-like complexes, and ATP synthases were all universally conserved. These data, coupled with phenotypic and biochemical information, suggest that these organisms oxidize H 2 outside the cytoplasmic membrane, reduce menaquinone, and generate a proton motive force for ATP synthesis. The most conserved sulfur reduction gene encoded a cytoplasmic NAD(P)H sulfur reductase. Genes encoding cytoplasmic hydrogenases and membrane-bound pyranopterin oxidoreductases were also common. The widespread conservation of menaquinol-dependent fumarate reductase points to CO 2 assimilation as another means of electron disposal, with excess reductant possibly used to drive sulfur or iron reduction. Understanding the metabolic potential of H 2 -dependent marine thermophiles deepens our knowledge of life in hydrothermal systems and contributes to the interpretation of data from ocean world missions.

food.title: Regulatory governance and full-scale digital transformation for prediction-based food safety management: Global trends and future perspectives
food.abstract: Background The global food safety paradigm is shifting from traditional, reactive hazard control toward proactive, predictive risk management to address increasingly complex supply chain vulnerabilities. However, current digital implementations remain fragmented, creating structural bottlenecks that hinder the transition to next-generation regulatory science. Scope and approach To our knowledge, this study provides one of the first comparative critical analyses of the HACCP-based data governance frameworks of six major jurisdictions. We compare jurisdictions in which private actors play a relatively larger role in certification and implementation ('market-led': the United States, the European Union, Canada, and Japan) with those in which public institutions play a dominant role ('state-led': South Korea and China), positioned along a governance continuum in which all systems combine public and private functions, focusing on their capacity for real-time risk prediction, public-private data integration, and global interoperability. Key findings and conclusions The market-led systems examined tend to foster food safety culture but are affected by 'Data Silos' that limit actions to retrospective tracebacks. The state-led systems examined may enhance data integrity but can create a 'Data Island' paradox due to an over-reliance on automating isolated physico-chemical Critical Control Points. To overcome these limitations, we propose a conceptual framework for Full-Scale Digital Transformation (Full DX). Converging prerequisite programs, structured food safety culture assessment (e.g., Shapley-FAHP), and intentional threat mitigations (TACCP/VACCP) into an interoperable predictive network powered by ensemble machine learning could support a more resilient regulatory…

food.title: Persistent biofilms in the food industry: Mechanistic insights, emerging interventions, and smart processing frontiers
food.abstract: Background Biofilms are a major microbiological concern in the food and beverage industry because microorganisms can attach to food-contact surfaces, processing equipment, and other industrial environments despite routine cleaning and sanitation. Once established, biofilms develop an extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix that provides structural stability and protection against mechanical removal, antimicrobial agents, and adverse environmental conditions. Their persistence can facilitate the survival and dissemination of microbial cells and spores, increasing the risk of cross-contamination, foodborne illness, spoilage, reduced shelf life, product recalls, and economic losses. Scope and approach This review provides a comprehensive overview of biofilms in food and beverage processing environments, focusing on mechanisms underlying biofilm formation and persistence, their implications for food safety and product quality, and their industrial significance. It focuses on major pathogenic and spoilage-associated microorganisms that form biofilms, such as Listeria monocytogenes , Salmonella , Escherichia coli , Pseudomonas , Staphylococcus aureus , Bacillus , Geobacillus , and Alicyclobacillus . The review further examines current approaches for biofilm detection and characterization and evaluates emerging anti-biofilm technologies, including ozone, cold plasma, bacteriophages, biosurfactants, nanotechnology, and multi-hurdle strategies. Key findings and conclusions Conventional sanitation may be inadequate against mature biofilms, highlighting the need for integrated monitoring and control. Emerging technologies show potential as alternative or complementary interventions. Key challenges remain in standardizing detection methods, understanding multispecies and…

food.title: Tracking respiratory syncytial virus dynamics in wastewater during the 2024–2025 season in Switzerland
food.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is responsible for a substantial health burden worldwide, particularly among children and older adults. In 2023, novel immunoprophylactic interventions for RSV were approved, underscoring the need to monitor circulating RSV lineages and detect mutations that could compromise intervention effectiveness. Here, we implemented wastewater-based genomic RSV surveillance by integrating digital PCR and amplicon-based sequencing within Switzerland's national wastewater monitoring program. We tracked RSV subtypes and individual mutations across the 2024-2025 peak season in six Swiss cities. RSV-A and RSV-B co-circulated nationwide, and both exhibited similar epidemiological dynamics estimated from their subtype-specific effective reproduction numbers. No previously reported F protein mutations relevant to prophylaxis efficacy were identified. Genetic diversity analysis of wastewater-derived sequences reflected patterns previously reported in clinical data, with higher diversity in RSV-A than RSV-B, and greater variability in the G compared to the F gene. food.title: Comparative transcriptomics reveals the electrosynthesis mechanisms of Sporomusa ovata under different reduction potentials
food.abstract: Understanding the metabolic mechanism of Sporomusa ovata is crucial for the practical applications of microbial electrosynthesis systems (MESs), a promising technology to sequester CO 2 . This study aims to investigate the electrosynthesis mechanisms of S. ovata under different cathodic potentials using comparative transcriptomics. As the cathodic potential became more negative from −0.4 to −0.7 V (vs standard hydrogen electrode [SHE]), acetate synthesis in MESs increased from 0.59 ± 0.05 to 6.03 ± 0.23 mM, while electron recovery efficiency decreased from 117.7 ± 6.8% to 52.5 ± 2.4%. Transcriptional analysis revealed that H 2 -mediated indirect extracellular electron uptake may be the core mechanism of S. ovata at −0.7 and −0.4 V. At both potentials, S. ovata relied on ATP synthesis from membrane hydrogenase-dependent respiratory chains. Compared with −0.4 V, upregulation of hydABC at −0.7 V enhanced cytoplasmic hydrogenase-based reducing power, dominating CO 2 fixation via the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway. Compared with −0.7 V, the transcriptional activity of membrane hydrogenase ( hupSL , hydA2B2 ) and higher expression of membrane electron transport components reflected the importance of the membrane-bound respiratory chain for S. ovata survival at −0.4 V. This work provides strategies for fine-tuning MESs to optimize energy efficiency and product specificity in sustainable biomanufacturing. Sporomusa ovata has been widely used as a cathode catalyst in MES research due to its extracellular respiratory capacity and two distinct H + -driven respiratory chains for chemolithoautotrophy. food.title: A Recall of Salt-Treated Fermented Canned Anchovies
food.abstract: This study describes the recall of salt-treated fermented canned anchovies (STFCAs) because of elevated histamine levels and bursting cans. STFCAs are a unique food item in that they are salt treated, fermented and canned, but not thermally processed. Thus, the mesophilic bacteria or bacterial spores, including those that can form histamine, are not destroyed by a thermal treatment. STFCAs have a limited shelf life due to a lack of a thermal inactivation step for the halophilic or proteinaceous bacteria, thus at the end of the shelf life the anchovy fillets can turn mushy in the can. Even though the STFCAs are held in an anaerobic environment during fermentation and after canning, and are not thermally treated, they are protected from Clostridium botulinum and Staphylococcus aureus growth and toxin formation by their elevated salt content and low water activity (a w ). The histamine forming bacteria (HFB) growth and sensorial degradation in the STFCAs can be limited with temperature control. We propose STFCAs should be held at or below 10°C (50°F) from manufacturing to consumption. We present calculated No Observed Adverse Effect Level (NOAEL) for STFCAs for the typical United States serving size of 15 g (∼1/2-oz), and discuss our proposed temperature control limit for transportation and storage of STFCAs [< 10°C (50°F)] in light of the lowered defect action level (DAL: 35 ppm) and action level (AL: 200 ppm) for histamine in seafood published by the US Food and Drug Administration in 2024. We suggest including the STFCAs in the regulatory exemption listed in CPG 540.525 ( FDA, 2024 ) for dried fish and fermented fish sauce/paste products that are intended for use only as condiments or as minor flavoring ingredients in other food products.

Elevated ozone reshapes wheat root-associated microbiomes through coordinated plant responses and rhizosphere environmental filtering
food.abstract: Elevated tropospheric ozone (O 3 ) threatens crop productivity, but how O 3 -induced changes in plant responses influence root-associated microbiomes remains unclear. We investigated the responses of microbial communities inhabiting the rhizosphere and root endosphere to elevated O 3 using four cultivars grown under ambient and 1.5-fold ambient O 3 in a field-based free-air O 3 -concentration enrichment (FACE) system. Plant traits, root-released organic carbon (ROC), rhizosphere properties, extracellular enzyme activities, and bacterial and fungal communities were jointly analyzed. Elevated O 3 reduced yield and root biomass, with cultivar-dependent changes in ROC. Elevated O 3 consistently increased rhizosphere pH and altered microbial resource allocation, increasing ecoenzymatic vector length by 4.1% and decreasing vector angle by 4.6%. Bacterial communities showed a stronger response than fungal taxonomic communities, particularly in the rhizosphere. However, variation partitioning indicated that soil properties, especially pH, rather than O 3 treatment alone, provided the strongest independent explanation for bacterial community variation. Fungal communities showed limited taxonomic turnover but exhibited shifts in predicted trophic guilds, including increased pathotroph- and saprotroph-associated groups and decreased symbiotroph-containing guilds under elevated O 3 . These results demonstrate that elevated O 3 reshapes the wheat root-associated microbiome through coordinated changes in plant performance, rhizosphere environmental filtering, and microbial functional strategies, highlighting the importance of plant-mediated processes in regulating belowground responses to atmospheric change. food.title: Evaluation of the mycobiota isolated from “Serrano” and Iberian ham as a potential agent to control ochratoxigenic moulds
food.abstract: Moulds are undesirable food contaminants. During the dry-cured ham ripening, surface moulds often develop beneficial to the final product. However, some species, such as Penicillium nordicum, P . verrucosum , and Aspergillus westerdijkiae , which frequently colonise dry-cured ham, produce mycotoxins, ochratoxin A (OTA). To control this hazard, native microorganisms have been proposed as a strategy. This study assessed the capacity of non-toxigenic indigenous yeasts and moulds to inhibit OTA production by ochratoxigenic moulds isolated from “Serrano” and feed-fed and acorn-fed Iberian hams. Biocontrol agents (BCAs), mainly comprising P. solitum , A . proliferans , and Debaryomyces hansenii , were selected and inoculated into ham agar containing a mixture of three ochratoxigenic P. nordicum strains. Samples for each ham type were incubated for two months under industrial curing conditions, divided into two phases (Maturations 1 and 2), mimicking the whole dry-cured ham ripening. The main difference between the maturation phases was that Maturation 1 had lower temperatures and higher relative humidity than Maturation 2. The highest significant OTA levels were found during Maturation 2 in all ham types, with environmental conditions (mainly temperature and water activity) being a key factor in the mycotoxin production. The BCAs consistently reduced OTA levels during both maturation stages compared with the non-treated control. Isolates obtained from feed-fed Iberian ham showed the highest efficacy, achieving mean OTA reductions of 94% and 91% for moulds and yeasts, respectively. Therefore, BCAs isolated from industry may limit OTA accumulation in feed-fed and acorn-fed Iberian hams.

food.title: Synergistic nisin–lysozyme treatment eliminates culturable cells in Listeria monocytogenes biofilms on stainless steel: a laboratory proof of concept for natural antimicrobial interventions
food.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes biofilms on stainless steel persist in ready-to-eat (RTE) food production because of their tolerance to conventional disinfection. This study evaluated nisin and lysozyme, two food-grade antimicrobials, against preformed L. monocytogenes biofilms (strains A1 and M5) on type 316 stainless steel at early (48 h) and mature (5-day) stages. Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) and working minimum biofilm eradication concentrations (MBEC w ; operational, assay-specific values giving no detectable culturable cells at 24 h and a ≥3-log reduction within 2 h) were determined. MBEC w /MIC ratios of 2–12 indicated biofilm-associated tolerance. Confocal microscopy showed thicker untreated biofilms at 5 days than at 48 h for M5 (27.3 to 36.0 μm) and, less clearly, for A1 (19.8 to 26.5 μm). Solid-surface checkerboard assays, expressed as Fractional Biofilm Eradication Concentration indices (FBECi), identified synergistic combinations (FBECi ≤ 0.5) that reduced counts below the detection limit (2.10 log 10 CFU/cm 2 ) within 2 h using only 6–25% (nisin) and 3–25% (lysozyme) of individual MBEC w values, a 75–97% reduction in antimicrobial usage compared with single agents. In regeneration assays, five of eight combinations showed no recovery of culturable cells within 24 h, under nutrient-rich conditions. Combined treatments reduced biomass and polysaccharide content more than single agents, compatible with, but not proof of, complementary action of lysozyme and nisin. These findings from an inert stainless-steel model suggest that nisin–lysozyme combinations warrant testing as a direct food-surface antimicrobial for RTE products, rather than as an equipment sanitiser; efficacy on biological surfaces remains to be established.

food.title: Scientific criteria and guidelines for identifying, reporting and interpreting omics data – transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and lipidomics – in meat science research
food.abstract: Omics approaches offer a rapidly expanding and highly valuable means to study meat science research questions associated with on-farm and post-farm activities. To help ensure the reliability, reproducibility, and transparency of these methodologies, this paper provides practical recommendations for identifying, reporting and interpreting transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and lipidomics studies in meat research with a focus on best practices regarding the experimental designs, data analysis, and interpretation of the results. Rather than restricting methodological innovation, these guidelines aim to establish recommended scientific criteria that enhance reproducibility, facilitate the integration of independently generated omics datasets through standardized reporting, compatible metadata and transparent analytical workflows among studies submitted to Meat Science journal. Although individual technologies continue to evolve, adherence to the key principles and criteria will substantially improve the scientific soundness and long-term impact of omics generated data applied to meat science research.

food.title: Molecular Detection of Horse and Goat Meat Using the mtDNA COI Gene in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
food.abstract: Meat adulteration is a growing concern because it compromises food authenticity, consumer confidence, and ethical or religious preferences. This study aimed to detect goat and horse DNA in meat marketed as goat meat in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, using mitochondrial cytochrome oxidase I (COI)-based polymerase chain reaction (PCR). A cross-sectional study was conducted from August 2025 to March 2026. A total of 427 raw meat samples were collected from licensed butcheries using a multistage random sampling approach. Genomic DNA was extracted using phenol-chloroform and salting-out methods and analyzed by conventional PCR using species-specific primers targeting the mitochondrial COI gene. A structured questionnaire was administered to assess meat-handler awareness of meat adulteration. Of the 427 samples analyzed, 368 (86.2%) were positive for goat DNA, whereas 5 (1.2%) were positive for horse DNA, indicating the presence of undeclared horse-derived genetic material. No amplification was detected in 54 (12.6%) samples, which were classified as inconclusive. Because only five samples were positive for horse DNA, statistical assessment of factors associated with horse DNA detection was not considered sufficiently reliable, and questionnaire findings are therefore presented descriptively. Awareness of meat adulteration was moderate, although the ability to identify adulterated meat by visual inspection alone was limited. Because the assay was qualitative, horse DNA could be detected but not quantified. These findings demonstrate the utility of COI-based PCR for meat species identification and support strengthening surveillance, laboratory capacity, and food authenticity monitoring systems in Ethiopia.

food.title: A UV mutant library reveals a link between mitochondrial genome loss and succinate production during wine yeast fermentation
food.abstract: The wine industry must adapt to new climatic and societal challenges. For this, selected yeast strains, mainly Saccharomyces cerevisiae, is a powerful lever, with ultra-violet (UV) mutagenesis used successfully to generate genetic diversity for strain improvement. From a library of 502 mutants, phenotyped in wine conditions, we identified a bimodal distribution of certain primary metabolites production. Using a multi-scale fermentation approach (15 mL screening, 250 mL validation and 1 L characterization), we compare 10 low and 10 high succinate producers, under wine-like conditions. Primary metabolite profiles differed markedly, particularly in the production patterns of tricarboxylic acid cycle intermediates, with a twofold and threefold differences in succinate and α-ketoglutarate production respectively. Pyruvate and α-ketoglutarate accumulated earlier in low-succinate-producing strains, whereas succinate production was delayed, occurring mainly after the stationary phase. These patterns suggest altered TCA activity and are consistent with a model in which early pyruvate and α-ketoglutarate accumulation precedes later succinate production, although this proposed pathway sequence was not directly measured. Genomic analysis of 5 high and 5 low succinate producers revealed complete absence of the mitochondrial genome, potentially resulting in the absence of the respiratory chain. However, mitochondrial genome loss cannot alone explain the phenotype, as UV mutagenesis may also have generated other genomic and genetic changes. Our results suggest an association between mitochondrial genome status and organic acid production. food.title: From chemical fingerprint towards authentication: UHPLC–Q-Orbitrap metabolomics reveals a phenylpropanoid-indole panel in Aroeira (Myracrodruon urundeuva) honey
food.abstract: Myracrodruon urundeuva (Aroeira) is a traditionally valued Brazilian monofloral honey with reported medicinal properties and growing commercial interest, yet robust chemical markers for its botanical discrimination remain unestablished. This study applied non-targeted UHPLC–Q-Orbitrap metabolomics, combined with stringent feature selection and semi-targeted analysis, to characterize the metabolic fingerprint of Aroeira honey and develop preliminary chemometric models for its characterization against selected Brazilian botanical origins (eucalyptus, citrus and wildflower). Twelve discriminant molecular features were identified based on accurate mass, isotopic abundance, retention time, and MS 2 fragmentation: nine phenylpropanoid-pathway metabolites and three indole-related compounds. Unsupervised analysis combined with univariate feature selection already provided unambiguous differentiation of Aroeira honey from all other botanical origins in this dataset, reflecting the chemically distinctive nature of this monofloral source. Supervised PLS-DA and one-class DD-SIMCA models further formalized this separation, demonstrating high classification performance on the test set. As a preliminary proof-of-concept, the proposed multi-marker panel and decision framework provide a promising and biologically interpretable tool for quality control of this distinctive Brazilian honey, though future studies with larger sample cohorts and external validation are necessary to confirm its broader applicability.

food.title: Species-dependent differences in aquaporin immunoreactivity in avian brain tissues
food.abstract: 1. Aquaporins are membrane water channel proteins that regulate cellular water transport while maintaining electrochemical gradients across cell membranes. This study investigated the expression patterns of aquaporins 1, 3, 4, 5, 9 and 11 brain tissues of Alectoris chukar, Coturnix coturnix and Gallus gallus domesticus using immunohistochemical and Western blot analyses. Astrocytic involvement was evaluated through Glial fibrillary acidic protein immunoreactivity.2. All examined Aquaporins were expressed in the brain tissues of all species, with clear species-dependent differences in expression intensity and distribution patterns. Aquaporin immunoreactivity was predominantly associated with vascular and perivascular structures across all species.3. Glial fibrillary acidic protein immunoreactivity showed a species-dependent pattern, indicating variability in astrocytic density and reactivity among the studied avian brains. The highest astrocytic involvement was observed in G. gallus domesticus, followed by A. chukar, while C. coturnix exhibited comparatively lower astrocytic reactivity. No sex-related differences were observed, which suggested that astrocytic distribution is primarily species-dependent rather than sex-dependent.4. These results showed a coordinated relationship between aquaporin expression and astrocytic architecture in the regulation of brain waterhomoeostasis. The species-specific differences reflected functional adaptations in avian neurovascular and astroglial systems.

food.title: Matrix-dependent growth and community dynamics of spoilage-associated lactic acid bacteria in weak organic acid salt-treated conventional and hybrid ready-to-eat chicken breast
food.abstract: Hybrid meat products are an emerging food category, but their microbial ecology during refrigerated storage remains poorly characterized. This study investigated the effects of commonly used weak organic acid salts on microbial community dynamics in conventional and hybrid uncured deli-style chicken breast products during refrigerated storage. Both product types were processed, packaged, inoculated with the same five-strain lactic acid bacteria (LAB) cocktail, and stored under identical conditions. LAB populations and pH were monitored, while bacterial community dynamics were characterized using Oxford Nanopore full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing, enabling high-resolution tracking of spoilage-associated taxa within the inoculated consortium over time and across treatments within matrix. Conventional and hybrid chicken breast exhibited distinct early taxonomic profiles and temporal shifts in microbial community composition within each matrix. LAB population responses to weak organic acid salt treatments differed between matrices over storage. At day 14, NaLD reduced LAB populations relative to the corresponding Control by approximately 1.59 and 1.27 log CFU/mL rinse in conventional and hybrid chicken breast, respectively, with a significant 0.32-log-CFU/mL-rinse difference between treatment effects ( P = 0.033). Sequencing further characterized treatment-associated microbial community dynamics within each matrix, with LAB predominating during later storage. Overall, these findings show that hybrid formulations can alter spoilage-associated taxonomic dynamics, including responses of the inoculated LAB consortium, even under the same processing and storage conditions, and underscore the need for matrix-specific validation of preservation strategies in hybrid meat…

food.title: Event-Based Surface-Water Connectivity Modeling of Leafy-Green Farm Exposure to Livestock-Associated Runoff
food.abstract: Recurring outbreaks of Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) associated with fresh produce have increased attention to preharvest contamination pathways, including the potential movement of material from livestock operations through surface water. We developed an event-based hydrologic screening framework to characterize relative livestock-associated runoff exposure for produce farms in the Salinas Valley, California. The framework combines rainfall-derived runoff estimates with modeled surface-water pathways connecting upstream livestock sources to downstream farms. Forty-eight rainfall events during 2018-2021 were evaluated, with runoff from livestock source areas estimated using the Curve Number method, a standard approach for estimating runoff from rainfall and land-surface characteristics. Source-to-farm connections were identified using terrain-based drainage routing. Upstream pasture contributions were reduced with increasing flow-path distance to represent decreasing source influence over longer travel paths. The resulting runoff-exposure metric represents relative hydrologic influence from connected upstream livestock sources and does not represent pathogen presence, concentration, contamination probability, or food-safety risk. Hydrologic routing identified 1,818 pasture-farm connections involving 277 downstream farms and 45 animal feeding operation (AFO)-farm connections involving 45 farms. Most farms (86.3%) had no modeled upstream pasture contribution under the baseline attenuation assumptions, and examples of farms intersecting pasture polygons but lacking routed downstream connections demonstrated that geographic proximity alone did not determine runoff-exposure. food.title: Interpretable discrimination of extra virgin olive oil adulteration using NIR and FTIR spectroscopy combined with PCA-SHAP analysis
food.abstract: Extra virgin olive oil (EVOO), a high-value product of the olive oil sub-sector, is vulnerable to economically motivated adulteration, creating a need for rapid and trustworthy quality-control tools across the agri-food chain. This study developed an interpretable spectroscopic strategy for distinguishing authentic EVOO from samples adulterated with sunflower oil, refined olive oil, and olive pomace oil. Near infrared (NIR) and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectra were reduced by principal component analysis (PCA) and modelled using six classifiers, including decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LGBM), support vector machine (SVM), and gradient boosting machine (GBM). Model performance was evaluated using a formulation-group-held-out prediction strategy within the controlled source oil system, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis, dependence plots, loading profiles, and interaction analysis were used for interpretation. The NIR-based RF model achieved the best prediction accuracy of 0.982, outperforming the best FTIR-based model with 0.821. SHAP analysis showed that the NIR model mainly relied on PC1, PC3, and PC4, which captured subtle multivariate variations across lipid-related NIR regions, indicating that the strongest absorption peaks were not necessarily the most discriminative features. In contrast, the FTIR model relied mainly on PCs associated with common triglyceride bands shared across oil categories, providing less class-specific information and partly explaining its weaker discrimination. The proposed PCA-SHAP framework supports transparent and chemically interpretable AI-based authentication of olive-derived agricultural products.
